Ita ex variis quasi elementis congregavit corpus unum populumque Romanum ipse fecit.

en: In the sixth century, the Roman empire began to pay an increasing amount of attention to Armenia. As part of his ambitious project to make Rome great again, the emperor Justinian created a new field army for Armenia, recruited soldiers there for the wars that he was waging on so many other fronts, and sought to co-opt segments of the Armenian aristocracy by bringing them to Constantinople and giving them offices. Initially, this produced oddities such as an Armenian officer, Gilakios, who led a unit of his countrymen in Italy but could not speak Greek or Latin, so when he was captured by the Goths he could state only his rank, which he had learned by heart after hearing it said many times. Also, the nobleman Artabanes, who had formerly waged war against the empire but had been brought onside, conceived the desire to marry Justinian’s niece, which, he thought, would give him a shot at the throne. Disappointed in this hope, he was approached by a relative, Arsakes, a scion of an Armenian princely house also resident in Constantinople, who was planning to assassinate Justinian.
zh: 在六世纪，罗马帝国开始越来越多地关注亚美尼亚。查士丁尼雄心勃勃，力图恢复罗马的强盛，为此，他为亚美尼亚新建一支野战军，也从当地招募兵士，让他们到各条战线作战，并试图通过招纳部分亚美尼亚贵族到君士坦丁堡，授予官职，以赢得他们的支持。起初这也造成了些奇事。例如，亚美尼亚军官吉拉基奥斯在意大利率领一支由同胞组成的部队，却不会讲希腊语或拉丁语，所以当他被哥特人俘虏时，他只能说出他的军衔——那是他在多次听人说过之后背下来的。还有，贵族阿尔塔巴尼斯，先前曾与帝国作战但已被笼络过来，萌生了娶查士丁尼侄女的愿望，他认为这会给他一个争夺皇位的机会。这一希望落空后，他的亲族阿尔萨克斯找上了他。阿尔萨克斯出自亚美尼亚一个王侯家族，当时也住在君士坦丁堡，正计划刺杀查士丁尼。

en: These stories were the preludes of a closer rapprochement between the empire and “Armenia,” which was a patchwork of states, provinces, and lordships. This relationship accelerated dramatically in the seventh century, when the empire was threatened by the caliphate and its access to old recruiting grounds in the central and western Balkans were cut off by the Slavs and Avars. The emperors turned increasingly to Armenia to recruit soldiers and officers for their armies and manpower for settlements and agriculture. This led to an influx of Armenians into the empire, including military units (sometimes stationed far from Armenia, for example in southern Italy);
fugitives from the wars with the Arabs who fled to Romanía;

captives brought back by the Roman armies; colonists who were resettled by the emperors in recaptured lands, such as the Peloponnese, Crete, Cilicia, and the small “Armenian themes” that began to proliferate along the frontier during the tenth century;

population drift, during the later tenth and eleventh centuries, from Armenia into the reconquered lands in Asia Minor; and the co-optation of aristocrats, their families, and retinues into the court hierarchy and imperial high command. Finally, in the late tenth and eleventh centuries, in a qualitative leap in expansion, the empire annexed Armenian realms, including Taron, Vaspurakan, and Ani (this will be discussed in detail in Chapter 7).
zh: 这些故事是帝国与“亚美尼亚”之间关系趋于密切的先声，此处的“亚美尼亚”是由多个政权、行省和领地组成的地域。双方的关系在七世纪迅速加深，当时帝国受到哈里发国的威胁，而斯拉夫人和阿瓦尔人又挡住了帝国前往巴尔干中部和西部传统募兵地区的道路。皇帝们越来越多地转向亚美尼亚，为他们的军队招募士兵和军官，为定居点和农业招募人力。这导致亚美尼亚人涌入帝国，包括调来的军队（有时驻扎在远离亚美尼亚的地方，例如南意大利）；
因与阿拉伯人交战而逃往罗曼尼亚的人；
罗马军队带回来的战俘；被皇帝们重新安置在收复土地上的殖民者，例如伯罗奔尼撒、克里特、基利家，以及十世纪开始沿边境大量出现的小“亚美尼亚军区”；
十世纪晚期和十一世纪期间从亚美尼亚逐渐迁往小亚细亚收复地区的人口；以及被招纳到朝廷及帝国军队指挥层的贵族及其家人与随从。最后，在十世纪晚期和十一世纪，扩张有了性质上的变化，帝国吞并了亚美尼亚诸国，包括塔隆、瓦斯普拉坎和阿尼（这将在第7章详细讨论）。

en: These events have been studied in many books and articles. In one crucial respect, however, our understanding of the presence of Armenians in the empire has been skewed by the logic of racial nationalism. I define the “Armenian fallacy” in Byzantine Studies as the assumption (which is rarely explicitly acknowledged) that Armenian identity was propagated genetically and could not be lost through cultural adaptation and assimilation. Put in the form of a syllogism: if
is an Armenian and
is descended from
, no matter how many generations have passed between them and no matter the admixture of any amount of what is called “non-Armenian blood,” then

is also “an Armenian.” This fallacy results in distortions, errors, and oversights. Specifically, it refuses to recognize the Roman cultural profile and ethnicity that many families and individuals acquired after living for a few generations in Romanía. It is thus predisposed to attribute an essentialized Armenian identity to individuals and families based on putative (and sometimes fictitious) “bloodlines.” It is unable to recognize that they had in the meantime become Roman, an identity that lacks the same existential weight in its eyes because it sees only blood. “Nationality” is here taken to be immutable, and linked to “stock,” that is, race.

Second, it assumes that Armenian blood prevails over the blood of non-Armenians, so the offspring of mixed marriages always “are” Armenians. At most, such people are called “of Armenian or partially Armenian origin,”
but the other “part” that makes up the whole is never named or researched; it does not reach the same level when it is conjoined with any “part” of Armenian “blood.”
zh: 这些事件已在许多书籍和文章中得到研究。然而在一个关键方面，我们对亚美尼亚人在帝国中活动的认识被种族民族主义的逻辑扭曲了。我把拜占庭研究中的“亚美尼亚谬误”定义为这样一种假设（很少被明确承认）：亚美尼亚身份由血统传递，无法因文化适应或同化而消失。用三段论的形式表述：如果
是亚美尼亚人，而
是
的后裔，无论他们之间经过多少代，无论掺入了多少所谓“非亚美尼亚血统”，那么
也“是亚美尼亚人”。这一谬误导致扭曲、错误和疏忽。具体而言，它拒绝承认许多家庭和个人在罗曼尼亚生活几代之后获得的罗马文化面貌和族群性。因此它倾向于根据所谓的“血统”给个人和家庭安上固定不变的亚美尼亚身份，而有些血统之说甚至出于虚构。它无法承认他们在此期间已变成罗马人——只看血统的人，觉得罗马身份没有同等的分量。“民族性”在这里被视为不可改变，并与“种系”即种族挂钩。
其次，它假设亚美尼亚血统压倒非亚美尼亚人的血统，所以混合婚姻的后代永远“是”亚美尼亚人。至多，这样的人被称为“亚美尼亚或部分亚美尼亚出身”，
但另一“部分”是什么，从没人指明、也没人研究。无论与多少亚美尼亚“血统”混合，另一部分从来得不到同等看待。

en: The hunt for Armenian bloodlines is a full-fledged modality of research in the field of Byzantine Studies. In 1905 and 1909, scholars such as G. Ter Sahakean and Z. N. Perperean published books on the “Armenian Byzantine Emperors,” extending western European modes of racial and nationalist historiography to the history of medieval Armenia. But their books were written in Armenian and so remained inaccessible. It was Nicholas Adontz, writing in French as well as in Armenian a few decades later, who made the search for Armenians in Byzantium into a more scholarly and less romantic nationalist process, though he too was often uncritical when it came to later medieval legends. Just like some of his sources, especially the eleventh-century historian Step’anos of Taron (also known as Asołik), Adontz saw Armenians everywhere and injected them into as many important events as he could. This might have remained a local national project had it not been endorsed a few decades later by Peter Charanis and Alexander Kazhdan.

The hunt for Byzantines who were “really” Armenians has been ongoing ever since, though in a number of individual cases there has been pushback against initially uncritical or unfounded claims. Nevertheless, among many scholars, making that connection has now become a knee-jerk reaction: the mere mention of certain names sparks an automatic qualification or subordinate clause labeling them as “Armenians” or as being “of Armenian descent,” even when that label or factoid is irrelevant to the discussion at hand or has no foundation in the sources.
zh: 对亚美尼亚血统的搜寻是拜占庭研究领域一套成形的研究范式。1905年和1909年，G·特尔·萨哈基安和Z·N·佩尔佩雷安等学者出版了关于“亚美尼亚拜占庭皇帝”的书籍，把西欧的种族和民族主义史学模式扩展到中世纪亚美尼亚的历史。但他们的书是用亚美尼亚语写的，因此一直无法被外界获取。几十年后用法语和亚美尼亚语写作的尼古拉斯·阿东茨，才使在拜占庭搜寻亚美尼亚人成为一个一种较重学术、较少浪漫民族主义色彩的研究，尽管他在涉及中世纪晚期传说时也常常不加批判。正如他的一些史料，尤其是十一世纪历史学家塔隆的斯捷潘诺斯（也称阿索利克），阿东茨到处看到亚美尼亚人，尽可能地把他们写进重要事件的叙述。这本来可能一直是一个局限于一地的民族主义项目，假如几十年后没有彼得·查拉尼斯和亚历山大·卡日丹的认可。
对“真正”是亚美尼亚人的拜占庭人的搜寻此后一直在进行，尽管在若干个案中，对最初不加批判或无根据的说法出现了抵制。尽管如此，在许多学者中，建立那种联系如今已成为下意识的反应：仅仅提到某些名字就有人不假思索地补上一句说明，把他们标为“亚美尼亚人”或“亚美尼亚后裔”，即使那个标签或琐闻与手头讨论无关，或在史料中没有根据。

en: This nervous tic is not today confined to nationalist Armenian historians; if it were, it might simply have been ignored along with the fantasies of other nationalist schools of historiography. The habit has spread widely in the field of Byzantine Studies. It has become the sort of thing that one

to say, for some reason, and sheer repetition has legitimized it over time. Seeing it done so commonly, one assumes that it must be a meaningful kind of thing to say, even though we are rarely told exactly what it means to say that a particular individual had Armenian “blood.” In one sense, this is a product of Roman denialism. Ethnic identities, especially if they bear the name of a modern nation, naturally seem more real and weighty than an insubstantial “Byzantine” identity that has been stripped of its Roman core. This cedes the field to modern nationalist ideologies, which step in to fill the vacuum. It is no wonder, then, that so many Byzantines have the label “Armenian” foisted upon them as their fixed ethnicity, when in fact they were just Romans, some of whose ancestors may have come from Armenia—or not, as we will see in many cases. As most scholars do not recognize the Romans of Byzantium as “real,” the drive to Armenianize Byzantium has expanded, seeking ever more frivolous, fictitious, flimsy, or far-fetched connections by which to label as “Armenians” a whole host of Romans, including many about whom no such claim is made in the sources.
zh: 今天，这种下意识的反应并不限于民族主义亚美尼亚历史学家；如果是那样，它本可以简单地连同其他民族主义史学流派的幻想一起被忽视。这一习惯已在拜占庭研究领域广泛传播。不知何故，提及亚美尼亚出身成了

的话，久而久之，反复出现本身就让这种说法显得理所当然。见得多了，人们以为这样说必定有意义，尽管我们很少被告知说某个特定个人有亚美尼亚“血统”究竟意味着什么。在某种意义上，这是罗马否认论的产物。族群认同，尤其如果它们冠有一个现代民族的名字，自然显得比一个被剥去罗马核心的、无实质的“拜占庭”认同更真实、更有分量。由此留下的空白，恰好让现代民族主义意识形态乘虚而入。那么难怪，如此多的拜占庭人被强加“亚美尼亚”标签作为他们固定的族群性，而事实上他们只是罗马人，其中一些人可能有亚美尼亚祖先。下文许多例子说明，就连这样的祖先也未必有据可查。由于大多数学者不承认拜占庭的罗马人为“真实的”，把拜占庭解释为亚美尼亚人的历史的倾向愈演愈烈，寻求越来越轻率、虚构、薄弱或牵强的联系，以便把一大群罗马人标为“亚美尼亚人”，包括许多史料中并未对其提出这种说法的人。

en: It is time for this nonsense to end. It has become a reflex that in most cases is meaningless or false. The present argument aims to bring balance between the Roman and Armenian sides of a centuries-long relationship, and specifically to restore integrity and historical weight to the Roman side of it. It leaves intact the integrity and continuity of the long history of the Armenian nation. To be clear: there absolutely were Armenians inside Romanía, by which I mean people who belonged to the wider Armenian people as that was defined by language, its own Church, principalities, local communities, aristocracy, cultural practices, collective memory, and ethnonyms, whatever variable forms those took—or by a partial combination of those factors. Conceivably, Armenian identity could survive the loss of one or two of these elements. For example, some Armenians belonged to Chalcedonian churches. There is no question that there were many Armenians of this kind throughout the empire, settled in minority communities or serving in the army. As we will see throughout this chapter, and especially at the end, the Romans definitely perceived them as a distinct people, and did not view them favorably overall (though there were exceptions).
zh: 这种荒唐的说法该结束了。它已成了下意识的反应，多半没有意义，或根本不实。这里的论述旨在重新平衡持续数百年的罗马与亚美尼亚关系，尤其要让罗马一方恢复其自身的完整性和历史分量。这丝毫无损于亚美尼亚民族悠久历史的完整与绵延。罗曼尼亚境内确有亚美尼亚人。我指的是亚美尼亚这一更广大民族的成员，无论他们凭借语言、本民族的教会、各公国、地方共同体、贵族、文化习惯、集体记忆和族名的哪些具体形式，或凭其中部分因素而归属于这个民族。即使其中一两项有所缺失，亚美尼亚身份也可能延续。例如，有些亚美尼亚人属于卡尔西顿派教会。毫无疑问，帝国各处都有许多这样的亚美尼亚人，定居于少数族群社群，或在军队服役。通读本章，尤其是最后一节，可以看到罗马人确实把他们视为一个有别于自身的民族，对他们总体评价也不高，尽管有例外。

en: But if Armenians stayed long enough in Romanía, especially if they lived and operated in small family groups, they could be assimilated just like everyone else. Over the course of a few generations and through intermarriage, Armenians could become mainstream Romans, whether or not they retained a memory of this one (Armenian) strand in their mixed ancestry. Instead of postulating fixed races, we should rather be thinking along the lines of a spectrum of assimilation, ranging from Armenians in Armenia or elsewhere who were not regarded as Romans; first-generation Armenian immigrants who had settled in Romanía or taken up imperial service; Armenians settled in the empire who were in the process of Romanization; Romans who remembered their Armenian ancestors; and Romans who had Armenian ancestors but did not know or care about that fact. To be sure, in most cases we lack sufficient information to make a precise classification, but a spectrum captures reality better than modern fictions about “blood.” We should add two more categories to it: Romans who had no Armenian ancestry but found it advantageous to claim that they did; and Romans who had no Armenian connection but have had it attributed to them by others, either by medieval historians or modern scholars. That last group is far larger than most historians realize.
zh: 但如果亚美尼亚人在罗曼尼亚待得足够久，尤其如果他们以少数家庭为单位生活和行动，他们也能像其他人一样被同化。在几代人的过程中并通过通婚，亚美尼亚人可以变成主流罗马人，无论他们是否保留对自己多种祖源中亚美尼亚这一支的记忆。考察同化的程度，可以看到一系列不同情况，包括在亚美尼亚或其他地方、不被视为罗马人的亚美尼亚人；定居于罗曼尼亚或开始帝国仕途的第一代亚美尼亚移民；定居于帝国、正在罗马化过程中的亚美尼亚人；记得他们亚美尼亚祖先的罗马人；以及有亚美尼亚祖先但不知道或不在乎那个事实的罗马人。诚然，在大多数情况下我们缺乏足够信息做精确分类，但按同化程度排列，比凭现代人虚构的“血统”区分更贴近实际。我们应该再加两个类别：没有亚美尼亚祖先，却觉得声称有这种祖先对自己有利的罗马人；以及没有亚美尼亚联系但被他人——无论是中世纪历史学家还是现代学者——归于这种联系的罗马人。最后那一群比大多数历史学家意识到的要大得多。

en: The fact of assimilation (i.e., Romanization) has often been recognized. It is, however, hard for the field to say exactly what it was that these Armenians were assimilating

We have to grasp for words and typically use the wrong ones because Byzantine Studies has never recognized Romanness as real. “Greek” is the usual stand-in for That Which Must Not Be Named, though it points weakly to language and not to nationality or ethnicity. For example, Armen Ayvazyan correctly pushed back against Romilly Jenkins’ racial view of the Byzantine aristocracy:
zh: 同化（即罗马化）的事实常常被承认。然而，拜占庭研究很难说清这些亚美尼亚人究竟
。学者不得不搜寻合适的字眼，却往往用错，因为这个领域从未认真看待罗马身份的真实性。“希腊”是人们惯用的代称，用来指那个避而不提的名字。说“希腊”也只让人依稀想到语言，说明不了民族或族群身份。例如，阿尔门·艾瓦兹扬有理由反对罗米利·詹金斯对拜占庭贵族的种族观点：

en: Much of [the] ethnically Armenian elite in the Byzantine Empire, in religious and cultural terms, was almost entirely Hellenized [i.e., Romanized] and certainly put imperial interests above the interests of Armenia, while retaining its connection with the Armenian nation only nominally, by and large for receiving a career support from their rich and powerful compatriots as well as getting authorization of their real or alleged noble origins from Armenian princely or even royal (Arsacid) blood.
zh: 拜占庭帝国里有亚美尼亚族群背景的精英中，相当一部分在宗教和文化上几乎已完全希腊化［即罗马化］，无疑把帝国利益放在亚美尼亚利益之上。他们只在名义上同亚美尼亚民族维持联系，通常是为了借助富有而有势力的同胞在仕途上获得支持，或借亚美尼亚王侯乃至王室（阿尔萨克王朝）的谱系坐实其真实或自称的贵族出身。

en: Nina Garsoïan likewise cautions that “the degree to which they were still to be considered ‘Armenian’ is open to question,” precisely because of assimilation, for which, when she is not typically calling it “Greek,” she once uses the unique word “Constantinopolization.”
She knows that within two or three generations they had the same profile as the rest of the aristocracy.

Some historians have used the correct term for this process: Werner Seibt has not only asked when is an “Armenian” just a normal Byzantine and when does he remain Armenian, he has coupled this question with an explicit acknowledgment of the integrative pull exerted by “the Romano-Greek national self-awareness” of Byzantium.
This explicit affirmation of a Roman

identity is language that Byzantinists lapse into when they just state what emerges clearly from the sources. The most recent statement on the issue, by Johannes Preiser-Kapeller, correctly denies that there is any point to labeling these people Armenians when their families had been in the empire for generations and had adopted an entirely “Roman” profile, but he still uses the typical scare quotes around the dreaded word.
zh: 尼娜·加尔索扬同样警告说，“他们仍应在多大程度上被视为‘亚美尼亚人’是值得质疑的”，原因正是同化。她通常称这一过程为希腊化，有一次则特别用了“君士坦丁堡化”一词。
她知道，在两三代内他们就有了与其余贵族相同的面貌。
一些历史学家用了这一过程的正确术语：维尔纳·赛布特不仅问一个“亚美尼亚人”何时只是一个正常的拜占庭人、何时他仍是亚美尼亚人，他还把这个问题与明确承认拜占庭的“罗马—希腊民族自我意识”具有使人融入的吸引力结合起来。
这种对罗马
认同的明确肯定，正是拜占庭学者如实陈述史料时会不自觉使用的措辞。关于这个问题最新的陈述，由约翰内斯·普赖泽—卡佩勒作出，正确地指出，当这些家族在帝国已生活数代，完全呈现出“罗马”面貌时，把他们叫作亚美尼亚人已经没有意义，但他仍在那个可怕的词周围用了典型的警示引号。

en: Despite such concessions, the Armenian fallacy remains strong in the field because its modalities and false premises have never been exposed. Even those who disagree with its general thrust (mentioned above) do not explicitly tackle its fundamental assumptions and preconceptions. The present chapter will continue the discussion initiated in Chapter 4, developing further the notion of Roman assimilation by focusing on the period between the seventh and the early tenth centuries (the imperial expansion of the tenth and eleventh centuries will be discussed separately under the rubric of “empire” in Chapter 7). I will argue that the scholarly trope according to which some Romans “were really” Armenians is a meaningless thing to say in most contexts, unless one holds a racial view of identity. It effaces Roman ethnicity for the benefit of a different, neighboring ethnicity that is construed along racial lines. Finally, going beyond the “melting pot” approach, I will consider how and why otherwise assimilated Romans may have maintained affective or symbolic memories of their Armenian ancestors. What were ethnic ancestors good for in Romanía?
zh: 尽管有这些让步，亚美尼亚谬误在这一领域仍然强大，因为这套写法及其错误前提一直未受揭示。即使那些不同意它总体倾向的人（上面提到的）也没有明确处理它的基本假设和先入之见。本章将延续第4章发起的讨论，着眼于七世纪至十世纪初，以进一步说明罗马式同化（十和十一世纪的帝国扩张将在第7章“帝国”标题下单独讨论）。我将论证，把某些罗马人说成“其实”是亚美尼亚人，在多数场合没有意义，除非说话者认定身份由种族决定。它为了一个沿种族路线建构的不同的、邻近的族群的利益，抹去了罗马族群性。最后，超越“熔炉”方法，我将考虑在其他方面已同化的罗马人如何以及为何可能保留对他们亚美尼亚祖先的情感或象征记忆。追溯外族祖先在罗曼尼亚有何用处？

en: Some Family Chronicles
zh: 几则家族史

en: The evidence allows us to track the assimilation of specific Armenian families only in the case of elites, whose members were visible at the highest levels of power in Romanía. Conversion to Byzantine Orthodoxy, intermarriage, dispersal, and assimilation would have affected nonelites as well, though it is likely that elites were assimilated faster and easier because they came in smaller groups (a family plus retinue), were not settled in compact communities, and intermarried more quickly with Romans. We are fortunate in this connection to possess the

children: Life of Saint Maria the Younger,

en: a saint whose family occupied the middle rungs of Roman provincial administration. The

is a family chronicle of sorts and offers a model of assimilation over the generations that we can use as a basic template. The author of the text was not trying to make a point about this process, but was instead concerned about a different set of (saintly) issues. Its basic narrative is therefore unlikely to be the product of politicized distortion.
zh: 凭现有证据，能追踪其同化历程的亚美尼亚家族只有精英家族，他们的成员出现在罗曼尼亚最高权力层中。普通人也会皈依拜占庭正教、与罗马人通婚，分散居住并逐渐同化，尽管很可能精英被同化得更快更容易，因为他们以更小的群体进来（一个家庭加随从），没有定居在紧凑的共同体中，而且更快地与罗马人通婚。幸而还有《小圣玛丽亚传》（Life of Saint Maria the Younger），其主人公的家族在罗马行省行政体系中身居中层。该传是一种家族编年史，提供了一个跨越数代的同化模型，我们可以用作基本模板。文本的作者并不是试图就这一过程表明一个观点，而是关心有关圣徒的另外一些问题。因此它的基本叙事不太可能是政治化扭曲的产物。

en: According to the

some powerful men of Greater Armenia emigrated to Constantinople during the reign of Basileios I (867–886), where they received honors and offices from the emperor. Among them was Maria’s father, who had two sons and two additional daughters. He managed to marry off the other two daughters before he died, but not Maria, who was raised by her mother (2). We do not know whether Maria was born in Armenia, but she was raised in Constantinople. We also do not know the ethnicity of her mother. If Basileios gave wives to these Armenian nobles (as Theophilos had to the Khurramites), then her mother might well have been Roman. In this case, Maria might not have learned to speak Armenian at all. She is never called “an Armenian” in the text: that fact about her ancestry is never mentioned again after the section about her father. Maria’s sister married a man named Bardas Bratzes, whose surname is the Armenian word for Georgian (i.e., Kartvelian, Greek “Iberian”). We do not know this man’s identity—he may have been a long-assimilated Roman—but his two names point to a mixed Caucasian background. The sister’s marriage was arranged by her father, the Armenian nobleman, so it seems that ethnicity may have played a role in the arrangement. But this was not to be in the case of Maria. Bardas Bratzes introduced her to a friend of his, Nikephoros, a
(mid-level officer) in the army, who went to Constantinople to ask her mother for Maria’s hand in marriage (2).
zh: 据该传，大亚美尼亚的一些有权势的人在瓦西里一世（867–886年在位）统治期间移民到君士坦丁堡，在那里他们从皇帝获得荣誉和官职。其中有玛丽亚的父亲，他有两个儿子和另外两个女儿。他生前为另两个女儿安排了婚事，玛丽亚当时尚未出嫁，由母亲抚养长大（2）。我们不知道玛丽亚是否出生在亚美尼亚，但她在君士坦丁堡长大。我们也不知道她母亲的族群性。如果瓦西里曾为这些亚美尼亚贵族安排婚事，就像狄奥斐卢斯曾为胡拉米派安排婚事那样，那么她的母亲很可能是罗马人。在这种情况下，玛丽亚可能根本没学会讲亚美尼亚语。她在文本中从未被称为“一个亚美尼亚人”：讲过她父亲的经历后，书里就再没有提她的祖源。玛丽亚的姐姐嫁给了一个名叫巴尔达斯·布拉茨斯的人，其姓氏是亚美尼亚语中“格鲁吉亚人”的意思（即卡特维尔人，希腊语称“伊比利亚人”）。我们不知道这个人的身份——他可能是一个早已同化的罗马人——但他的名和姓都指向高加索，但来源不一。姐姐的婚姻由她父亲、那位亚美尼亚贵族安排，所以似乎族群性可能在安排中起了作用。但玛丽亚的情况并非如此。巴尔达斯·布拉茨斯把她介绍给他的一个朋友尼基弗鲁斯，军队中的一个
（droungarios，中级军官），后者到君士坦丁堡向她母亲求娶玛丽亚（2）。

en: There was nothing Armenian or ethnic about Nikephoros. His siblings were named Alexios and Helene, and Helene’s daughter was named Sophia (7, 21). Everyone in this story, moreover, is Byzantine Orthodox and speaks Greek. Maria and her husband Nikephoros lived in the Thracian town of Vizye, among other Romans (until he caused her death). That is where the couple made their life together. When Maria identifies herself to a painter in a posthumous vision, she calls herself “Maria from Vizye,” not Maria the Armenian (18). When a priest later tells her story to the Bulgarians, he says that “she was from Constantinople, the daughter of noble parents” (24). The Bulgarian later calls her Maria of Vizye (25). Maria and Nikephoros had four children, whose names alternated between Greek and Armenian, which indicated an affective memory of Maria’s Armenian past (Orestes and Bardanes, who both died young, and the twins Stephanos and Baanes: 4–6). Stephanos eventually became a monk with the name Symeon, while Baanes, like his father, had a military career. He rose to become “the commander of the army of the Romans” at Selymbria (24–25). When finally there was peace between the Romans and Bulgarians, “everyone rushed to his own fatherland

” so Baanes returned to Vizye (27). This man was just a Roman: a Greek-speaking, Orthodox captain in the Roman army whose home was a Roman town in Thrace. He married a woman from a distinguished family (30). It makes no sense to call any of the people in this story Armenians, except for the immigrants under Basileios I. This is “melting pot” assimilation, with some tinges of affective ethnicity (to be discussed below).
zh: 尼基弗鲁斯身上没有任何亚美尼亚或其他外族背景的迹象。他的兄弟姐妹名叫阿莱克修斯和海伦妮，而海伦妮的女儿名叫索菲娅（7、21）。此外，这个故事里的每个人都是拜占庭正教徒，都说希腊语。玛丽亚和她的丈夫尼基弗鲁斯住在色雷斯的维济耶镇，与其他罗马人同住（直到他导致了她的死亡）。这对夫妇就是在那里共同生活的。当玛丽亚在一次身后异象中向一位画家表明身份时，她自称“来自维济耶的玛丽亚”，而非亚美尼亚人玛丽亚（18）。后来一位祭司向一位保加尔人讲述她的故事时，说“她来自君士坦丁堡，父母皆出身名门”（24）。那位保加尔人后来称她为维济耶的玛丽亚（25）。玛丽亚和尼基弗鲁斯有四个孩子，孩子们的名字轮番采用希腊语和亚美尼亚语，表明家人还珍视玛丽亚的亚美尼亚家世（俄瑞斯忒斯和巴尔达尼斯，两人都早夭，以及双胞胎斯特凡诺斯和巴阿尼斯：4–6）。斯特凡诺斯最终出家为僧，法名西美昂，而巴阿尼斯则像他父亲一样从军。他升任塞林布里亚的“罗马人军队的统帅”（24–25）。当罗马人与保加尔人之间终于实现和平时，“人人都奔回自己的故土（patris）”，于是巴阿尼斯回到了维济耶（27）。此人就是个罗马人：罗马军队中一位说希腊语的正教军官，家在色雷斯的一座罗马城镇。他娶了一位出身显赫家族的女子（30）。除了瓦西里一世治下的那些移民，把这个故事中的任何人称为亚美尼亚人都说不通。这是“熔炉”式的同化，同时也留有一点对祖先族群的感情（下文将讨论）。

en: The Armenian fallacy would have us believe that Baanes’ (hypothetical) grandchildren “were” Armenians. We will scrutinize the operations of this racial logic in a later section. Let us first consider some additional genealogies.
zh: 亚美尼亚谬误要让我们相信，巴阿尼斯（假设的）孙辈“就是”亚美尼亚人。我们将在后面一节仔细审视这种种族逻辑的运作。先让我们再看一些别的家系。

en: Ioseph Genesios was a historian of the mid-tenth century who wrote an account,

children: On the Reigns of the Emperors,

en: covering most of the ninth century in what he believed was high-style Greek, and he dedicated it to Konstantinos VII. Genesios was an Orthodox Roman: he speaks of Romans in the first-person plural and identifies with the Roman order.
It is almost certain, moreover, that Genesios’ grandfather was the ninth-century high official Konstantinos, who appears many times in the work.
Genesios goes out of his way to praise this man and highlights his deeds more than do other sources. He also knows more about his family background than do the others:
zh: 约瑟夫·格内西奥斯是十世纪中叶的一位史家，他用自认为高雅的希腊语撰写了《论诸帝统治》（On the Reigns of the Emperors），记述九世纪大部分时间里的历史，并把它献给了君士坦丁七世。格内西奥斯是个正教罗马人：他用第一人称复数谈论罗马人，并认同罗马秩序。
此外，几乎可以肯定，格内西奥斯的祖父就是九世纪的高级官员君士坦丁，此人在书中多次出现。
格内西奥斯特意褒扬此人，比其他史料更突出他的事迹。他也比其他人更了解此人的家世背景：

en: Konstantinos was said to be of Armenian descent (ἐξἈρμενίων . . . ἀπόγονον Ἀρμενίων) and was sent to Theophilos [829–842] by his relatives and the rulers of his native land as a hostage and ambassador. Shortly afterwards, on account of the beauty of his soul and body and his noble disposition in all great affairs, he was appointed
of the

zh: 据说君士坦丁是亚美尼亚裔（ἐξἈρμενίων . . . ἀπόγονον Ἀρμενίων），被他的亲属和他故土的统治者们作为人质兼使节送到狄奥斐卢斯［829–842］那里。不久之后，由于他灵魂与肉体的俊美，以及他在一切重大事务中表现出的高贵禀性，他获任
（arithmos）的
（droungarios），即帝国
（vigla）卫队的指挥官；后来他被授为帕特里基奥斯（patrikios），最终出任驿道总监（logothetes of the dromos）。

en: Konstantinos thus appears to be the exact Armenian analogue to Theophobos, the son of the leader of the Khurramites who was sent to the Roman court to be raised there, learn Roman ways, and serve as a diplomatic bridge. In both cases, these “hostages” stayed in Romanía and had distinguished careers there.

We note again the use of moralizing language—“the beauty of his soul and body and his noble disposition”—to counter any foreignness that might be imputed to this man. Moreover, Genesios does in one place call him “the Armenian,” but he and his parallel source, the
sometimes phrase this more carefully: he was “from the Armenians,” “was descended from Armenians,” or “his
was derived from the Armenians.”
These were roundabout expressions to designate his
but not who he was in the present.
zh: 因此，君士坦丁看来与狄奥福波斯有着极为相似的经历——后者是胡拉米派首领之子，被送到罗马宫廷，在那里被抚养长大、学习罗马方式，并充当外交桥梁。在这两个事例中，这些“人质”都留在了罗曼尼亚，并在那里成就了显赫的仕途。
我们再次注意到那种道德化措辞的使用——“他灵魂与肉体的俊美，以及他的高贵禀性”——用来消除人们可能对他外族出身的偏见。此外，格内西奥斯确实在一处称他为“那个亚美尼亚人”，但他和与之平行的史料《瓦西里一世传》（Life of Basileios I）有时措辞更为谨慎：他“出自亚美尼亚人”，“是亚美尼亚人的后裔”，或“他的族类（genos）源自亚美尼亚人”。
这些委婉的说法谈的是他的
，和他当时的身份有别。

en: Konstantinos’ two sons were Genesios (not the historian, but his uncle) and Thomas, a high official at the court in the early tenth century, described by the
as “philosophical and incorruptible.”
It is probable that our historian Genesios was Thomas’ son. Genesios is labeled by a later historian as a “Byzantine,” that is, a Constantinopolitan.

He exhibits in his own work no special attachment to Armenians, whom he mentions as neutrally as any other foreign people. One passage, however, is interesting. When he refers to the Armenian origins of the emperor Leon V (813–820), Genesios digresses to divulge an antiquarian (and fictional) etiology according to which “the Armenians took their name from Armenos, who was from the Thessalian city of Armenion, and had campaigned with Jason.”

This is not much to go on, but it may reflect a desire on the part of a man who had a bit of Armenian ancestry to ameliorate its potential foreignness by linking Armenians to an ancient Greek hero who served on the

It is as much affective-ethnic attachment as we would expect from a third-generation Roman. Other Genesioi are attested in the later tenth and early eleventh centuries—a branch of them were prominent citizens of the city of Trebizond— but they are never called Armenians, and it is not certain anyway that they were descended from Konstantinos.

At any rate, Armenian origins are mentioned only for Konstantinos, the first to arrive, and even in his case they are oblique, for it is possible that he was raised in Constantinople. Unfortunately, we know nothing about the women of this family, who would have played a key role in changing its ethnic profile over the generations.
zh: 君士坦丁的两个儿子是格内西奥斯（不是那位史家，而是他的叔父）和托马斯——后者是十世纪初宫廷中的一位高级官员，《瓦西里一世传》（Life of Basileios I）称他“富于哲思、清廉不阿”。
很可能我们这位史家格内西奥斯就是托马斯之子。一位较晚的史家给格内西奥斯贴上了“拜占庭人”的标签，也就是君士坦丁堡人。
他在自己的著作中对亚美尼亚人并无特别的依恋，提到他们时与提到任何其他外族一样中立。不过有一处颇有意思。当他谈及皇帝利奥五世（813–820）的亚美尼亚起源时，格内西奥斯岔开去透露一则考古溯源的虚构传说，据说“亚美尼亚人得名于阿尔梅诺斯，此人来自色萨利的阿尔梅尼翁城，曾随伊阿宋出征”。

单凭这一点还很难下判断，但它可能反映了这样一个带有少许亚美尼亚血统的人的一种愿望：通过把亚美尼亚人与一位曾在阿尔戈号（Argo）上服役的古希腊英雄相联系，来淡化其潜在的异邦性。一个移民家族第三代的罗马人，对祖先的族群有这样程度的情感联系，并不出人意料。十世纪后期和十一世纪初还见有其他格内西奥斯家族成员——其中一支是特拉比松城的显赫公民——但他们从未被称为亚美尼亚人，而且无论如何也不能确定他们是君士坦丁的后裔。
无论如何，只有最早到来的君士坦丁被提及有亚美尼亚出身，就连他的出身也说得含糊，因为他有可能是在君士坦丁堡长大的。遗憾的是，我们对这个家族的女性一无所知，而她们本应在世代之间改变其族群面貌的过程中扮演关键角色。

en: A snapshot of the same progression—from ancestor of qualified Armenian origin to just plain Roman descendant—can be observed in the case of the Mosele family (Μωσηλέ or Μουσελέ, spelled variously, derived from Armenian Mušel). The first known to us is Alexios, who held court titles and military commands and was involved in imperial politics at the highest level in 790. The chronicles, sparse for this period, do not call him an Armenian; for all we know, his family may have moved to Romanía many generations previously. Alexios appears to be a fully integrated member of the Roman high command.
The same is true of the next one known to us, also named Alexios, who was active at the court of Theophilos (829–842), married the emperor’s daughter, and was appointed

a rank held only by those who were close to the imperial family. This Alexios is called “an Armenian” in one source, while another gives a detailed background: “He was descended from the race of the Krenitai, a place in the land of the Armenians. . . . He lived on the acropolis [of Constantinople] in the so-called manor house of the Krenitissa woman.”

Juan Signes Codoñer has plausibly linked the Krenitai to the Armenian city of Karin (Roman Theodosioupolis), which was captured by Konstantinos V in 754; an Armenian source relates that Konstantinos V took a large part of the local population back to the empire and resettled them there. Interestingly, the emperor Theophilos, Alexios’ father-in-law, also attacked Karin in the 830s, forcing the city to pay tribute. A local link would have been an asset in this expansion.
zh: 在莫塞莱家族（Μωσηλέ 或 Μουσελέ，拼写不一，源自亚美尼亚语 Mušel）的事例中，可以观察到同一进程的剪影——祖先的亚美尼亚出身尚须加以限定，后代则已完全是罗马人。我们所知的第一位是阿莱克修斯，他拥有朝廷头衔和军职，并于790年在最高层参与了帝国政治。这一时期的编年史记载稀少，并未称他为亚美尼亚人；就我们所知，他的家族可能在许多代以前就已迁居罗曼尼亚。阿莱克修斯看来是罗马最高统帅部中一名完全融入的成员。
我们所知的下一位也是如此，他同样名叫阿莱克修斯，活跃于狄奥斐卢斯（829–842）的宫廷，娶了皇帝的女儿，并被授为凯撒（kaisar）——这一尊位只有与皇室亲近者才能拥有。这位阿莱克修斯在一部史料中被称为“一个亚美尼亚人”，而另一部则给出了详细的背景：“他出自克雷尼泰人的族系，那是亚美尼亚人之地的一处地方……他住在［君士坦丁堡］卫城上所谓克雷尼提萨妇人的宅邸里。”
胡安·西格内斯·科多涅尔合理地把克雷尼泰人与亚美尼亚城市卡林（罗马时期的狄奥多西乌波利斯）联系起来，该城于754年被君士坦丁五世攻占；一部亚美尼亚史料记述，君士坦丁五世把当地人口的很大一部分带回帝国，并在那里重新安置。有意思的是，阿莱克修斯的岳父狄奥斐卢斯皇帝也在830年代进攻过卡林，迫使该城纳贡。在这一扩张中，如果在当地有联系，自然有利于这场扩张。

en: The particulars need not detain us here, and other scholars may interpret the place-name Krenitai differently. What we seem to have here is a man active at the highest level of imperial service, who was perfectly assimilated (certainly by language, religion, marriage, and residence) but found it advantageous, in the early ninth century, to remind people of his (ostensible) Armenian ancestry and to live in a manor named after his native land, a form of affective attachment. None of this made Alexios “an Armenian.” Rather, he was a Roman who wanted to be seen as ethnically inflected, probably for political reasons. He was possibly two or three generations out from his Armenian ancestors. Later members of the family, prominent in the tenth century, were even further removed from this ethnic origin. An Alexios Mosele was an admiral in 922 and his (likely) son was the
Romanos Mosele (mid-tenth century). None of the many sources that mention them call them Armenians in any way or hint at their foreign origin or distinctive cultural profile.
zh: 细节不必在此纠缠，其他学者对克雷尼泰这个地名也可能有不同解读。我们这里似乎看到的是这样一个人：他活跃于帝国仕途的最高层，已完全被同化（至少在语言、宗教、婚姻和居住方面如此），却在九世纪初觉得，提醒人们注意自己（据称）的亚美尼亚祖源、并住在一座以其故土命名的宅邸里，对自己有利——这是一种情感依恋的形式。这一切都没有使阿莱克修斯成为“一个亚美尼亚人”。他是罗马人，却希望别人也看到他有不同的族群背景，很可能是出于政治原因。他距离他的亚美尼亚祖先可能已有两三代。这个家族较晚的成员在十世纪声名显赫，与这一族群起源就更加疏远了。一位阿莱克修斯·莫塞莱在922年担任海军统帅，行政长官（magistros）罗曼努斯·莫塞莱（十世纪中叶）很可能是他的儿子。提及他们的众多史料，没有一部以任何方式称他们为亚美尼亚人，或暗示他们的异邦起源或独特的文化面貌。

en: Another surname that indicated an Armenian ancestry was Taronites, referring to the mostly Armenian realm of Taron that was ceded to the empire around 968 by the sons of its last native ruler, Ašot III. They took the name Taronites and were appointed to high military posts. To be sure, not all men with the surname Taronites were necessarily descended from its former ruling family, as anyone who moved from Taron to Romanía could call himself Taronites, but whether there were one or more lines does not concern us here. The Taronites rose to the highest levels of the Roman aristocracy in the eleventh and twelfth centuries. They certainly became Byzantine Orthodox and dropped their native names (whose Greek versions were Pankratios, Asotios, and Krikorikios) in favor of standard Roman names: Romanos, Theophylaktos, Michael, Gregorios, Eirene, and others.

They also intermarried with prominent members of the Roman and former Bulgarian aristocracies. The literary record about their later activities contains no references to their foreign origin, other than that encoded in their surname, and it also leaves no doubt that they became normal (if elite) Romans. A Taronites is listed among the “Roman” casualties of a battle with the Turks in 1070.

At the end of the eleventh century, Theophylaktos of Ohrid wrote letters to Gregorios Taronites, praising his accomplishments as an administrator and governor who defeated the Franks and the Turks: now, he says with a flourish, it will be seen that those celebrated trophies of the ancient Romans were no myth, as we have among us precisely such a most noble Roman; that ancient Roman spirit is not dead but lives on in you.
zh: 另一个表明亚美尼亚血统的姓氏是塔隆尼特斯，它指向以亚美尼亚人为主的塔隆王国——该王国约在968年由其最后一位本土统治者阿绍特三世的儿子们割让给帝国。他们采用了塔隆尼特斯这个姓，并被授以高级军职。诚然，并非所有姓塔隆尼特斯的人都必然出自其昔日的统治家族，因为任何从塔隆迁居罗曼尼亚的人都可以自称塔隆尼特斯，但究竟有一支还是多支世系，与此处的讨论无关。塔隆尼特斯家族在十一、十二世纪攀升到罗马贵族的最顶层。他们无疑成了拜占庭正教徒，并放弃了本土名字（其希腊语形式为潘克拉提奥斯、阿索提奥斯和克里科里基奥斯），改用标准的罗马名字：罗曼努斯、塞奥菲拉克托斯、米海尔、格里戈里奥斯、伊琳娜等等。
他们还与罗马贵族及前保加尔贵族的显赫成员联姻。关于他们后期活动的文献记载，除了姓氏所保留的来历，没有任何对其异邦起源的提及，而且也毫不含糊地表明他们已经和一般罗马人无异，尽管地位显赫。一位塔隆尼特斯被列入1070年与突厥人一场战役的“罗马”阵亡者名单。
十一世纪末，奥赫里德的塞奥菲拉克托斯致信格里戈里奥斯·塔隆尼特斯，褒扬他作为行政官和总督击败法兰克人与突厥人的功业：他以夸饰的笔调说，如今人们将看到，古罗马人那些著名的战功并非神话，因为我们中间恰恰就有这样一位最高贵的罗马人；那古罗马的精神并未死去，而是活在你身上。

en: Alexios I Komnenos appointed one Ioannes Taronites to a provincial post in 1107, and the description of this man by Anna Komnene reveals a perfectly Romanized gentleman:
zh: 阿莱克修斯一世·科穆宁于1107年任命一位约安尼斯·塔隆尼特斯担任地方官职，而安娜·科穆宁娜对此人的描述展现了一位完全罗马化的绅士：

en: From his early childhood [Ioannes] had been under the emperor’s protection and for a long time served him as a secretary. He was a man of active mind, with a sound knowledge of Roman law. . . . If he spoke freely, his censures were not devoid of tact: he was [Aristotle’s] ideal of what a dialectician should be.
zh: ［约安尼斯］自幼年就受到皇帝的庇护，并长期担任他的秘书。他是个头脑敏锐的人，对罗马法有扎实的了解……他即使直言批评，也有分寸，正是［亚里士多德］心目中理想的辩证论者。

en: It is absurd to refer to such people as “Greek-speaking Armenians.”

We have a nuptial poem from the mid-twelfth century celebrating the marriage of a Taronitissa bride to a scion of the ruling Komnenos dynasty, who is hailed as the pinnacle of Roman manliness. The girl apparently also had some Komnenian ancestry, so the poet, addressing the groom, says that “the maiden is not from a foreign race (φυλὴ ἀλλοδαπή) but from a
related to your father’s and a kinclan,” while simultaneously being “the glory of the Taronites” and “from a noble family.”
It did not get more Roman than this. The Taronites were a benchmark of Romanness, and no mention is made anywhere in the poem of a foreign origin.
zh: 把这样的人称为“说希腊语的亚美尼亚人”是荒谬的。
我们有一首十二世纪中叶的贺婚诗，为嫁入当朝科穆宁家族的一位塔隆尼特斯家族女子所作，后者被誉为罗马男子气概的巅峰。这位姑娘显然也有某种科穆宁血统，于是诗人对新郎说，“这位少女并非出自异族（φυλὴ ἀλλοδαπή），而是出自与你父亲那一支有亲的
（genos），是你家的亲族”，同时她又是“塔隆尼特斯家族的荣耀”且“出身名门”。
这是再典型不过的罗马人了。塔隆尼特斯家族是罗马性的一个标杆，而诗中任何地方都没有提到异邦起源。

en: The families of Maria the Younger, Konstantinos “the Armenian,” Mosele, and Taronites demonstrate the pace, modes, and extent of Armenian integration into Roman society. Ethnic affiliations attach to the first generation of new arrivals, then give way to only symbolic-affective gestures (the names of children or manor houses), and finally disappear entirely. To be sure, these were all elites (or subelites, in the case of Maria) who sought advancement in Roman imperial service through offices, marriages, and the politics of patronage. Matters would have been different among groups of Armenians resettled in provincial villages. It is possible that such small communities retained their Armenian identity for centuries, though they too could be assimilated if they were dispersed among the Roman population and given strong incentives. Kazhdan opined that Armenian communities in the empire were close-knit, allowing them to retain a sense of ethnic distinctiveness.
But the proof for this is weak.

Usually, it is negative: a group is mentioned as being settled in a particular location, but is never heard from again. Moreover, Armenian authors evince almost no interest in their compatriots who moved to the empire, whether in groups or as individuals. In part, this may be because Armenian historiography placed a premium on confessional affiliation and increasingly refused to recognize as true Armenians those who joined Chalcedonian churches, which many of them did, especially if they “went Roman.”
Thus, it is difficult to reconstruct networks linking Roman elites of Armenian descent to their counterparts in Armenia.
zh: 小圣玛丽亚、“亚美尼亚人”君士坦丁、莫塞莱和塔隆尼特斯这些家族，展示了亚美尼亚人融入罗马社会的速度、方式与程度。族群身份在第一代迁入者身上还看得出来，到后来只在孩子或宅邸的名字中留下一点情感寄托，最终完全消失。诚然，这些都是精英（玛丽亚一家地位稍低），他们通过官职、婚姻和庇护关系在罗马帝国仕途中谋求晋升。在被重新安置到外省村庄的亚美尼亚人群体中，情况会有所不同。这样的小共同体有可能保留其亚美尼亚认同达数世纪之久，不过如果它们被分散到罗马人口之中并被给予强有力的激励，也同样可能被同化。卡日丹认为，帝国境内的亚美尼亚共同体关系紧密，使其得以保留一种族群独特感。
但这一点的证据是薄弱的。
相关推断往往以史料的沉默为依据：某个群体被提到安置在某地，此后便再无音讯。此外，亚美尼亚作者对那些迁居帝国的同胞——无论成群还是单独——几乎毫无兴趣。这部分可能是因为亚美尼亚史学高度重视教派归属，并越来越拒绝把那些加入卡尔西顿派教会的人承认为真正的亚美尼亚人，而他们中许多人都这样做了，尤其是当他们“成了罗马人”的时候。
因此，要重建把亚美尼亚裔罗马精英与他们在亚美尼亚的对应人物联系起来的网络，是困难的。

en: The Armenian fallacy, however, primarily mischaracterizes not so much groups (which are virtually invisible) as it does individuals, and their decisions. As these individuals are mostly elites, it is on them that we must focus.
zh: 亚美尼亚谬误主要歪曲的是个人及其选择。群体几乎没有在史料中留下踪迹，而这些个人大多属于精英阶层，正是我们接下来要考察的人。

en: The Fallacy in Action
zh: 谬误如何运作

en: The Armenian fallacy consists of interconnected and expanding errors. It began by imputing racial-ethnic labels to various Romans on the basis of an alleged ancestry. No number of intervening generations or mixed marriages sufficed to stop the transmission of a fixed Armenian identity through a single bloodline. This approach gained a foothold in part because no scholars were willing to push back on behalf of Byzantine Romanness, which the field has never recognized as such, whereas Armenians were and still are a real nation. Once this axiom was accepted, it began to chew almost methodically through Roman history to find “Armenians” everywhere, expanding like an economic bubble into increasingly riskier and attenuated claims. Armenian identity is now postulated not only on the basis of actual textual claims about a person’s ancestry— whatever value we may place on those—but also on the basis of a name, place of origin (anywhere in the eastern provinces of the empire would do), collateral relations, in-laws, friendships, and alliances. Any link, no matter how tenuous, now serves to make one into “an Armenian.” Finally, once networks of these alleged “Armenians” were established, historians then began to attribute specific acts and behaviors to the underlying ethnic bond among them, racializing their politics.
zh: 亚美尼亚谬误由一系列相互关联、不断扩张的错误构成。它起初依据传说中的世系，把种族—族群标签强加于各类罗马人。无论中间隔了多少代、多少次通婚，都不足以阻止一种固定的亚美尼亚认同通过单一血脉传递。这种做法之所以站稳脚跟，部分原因在于没有学者愿意为拜占庭的罗马性提出异议，因为学界一直不承认这种身份，而亚美尼亚人过去是、现在仍是一个真实的民族。一旦这一公理被接受，这种做法就近乎有条不紊地搜遍了罗马史，到处寻找“亚美尼亚人”，像一个经济泡沫那样扩张，提出越来越冒险、越来越牵强的论断。如今，亚美尼亚认同的设定不仅依据关于某人血统的实际文本陈述——无论我们赋予这些陈述多大价值——还依据一个名字、出身地（帝国东部行省的任何地方都算）、旁系亲属、姻亲、友谊和联盟。任何关联，无论多么微弱，如今都被用来把一个人变成“一个亚美尼亚人”。最后，一旦这些据称的“亚美尼亚人”的网络被建立起来，史家们便开始把具体的行动和行为归因于他们之间潜在的族群纽带，从而把他们的政治种族化。

en: This is a house of cards. We have seen that even explicit attributions of Armenian ethnicity in the primary sources may not mean much when it comes to the identity of individuals. Clearly, they meant something or else they would not have been remembered, recorded, or invented, but their existential valence may have been quite different from how they are used in scholarship. Consider the significance of personal names. Prominent men in Byzantine history are often—and in some cases always—labeled as Armenians if they bear a name that was common in Armenia, or which can be etymologized as a calque, translation, or even a distortion of an Armenian name, resulting in some remarkably far-fetched connections that are proffered with a straight face only because the underlying illogic of the fallacy has taken such a strong hold in the field. This methodology of “ethnicity by name” persists even though it has correctly been recognized as problematic.

Armenian names such as Bardas and Bardanes were popular and fashionable within Roman society, just as Germanic names had been fashionable between the fourth and sixth centuries and for largely the same reasons: with Armenian noblemen taking positions of military and political leadership, their names became prestigious for Romans. This had happened in previous Roman tradition too, with Etruscan, Oscan, Greek, and other names. The consul of 56 bc, Lucius Marcius Philippus, was not a “Greek.” Emperors named Michael and John were not Jews. The states of Massachusetts and Ohio are not more “Indian” than New York and Pennsylvania, and John F. Kennedy was not an Irishman.
zh: 这是一座纸牌屋。我们已经看到，即便是原始史料中明确认定某人是亚美尼亚人，就个人认同而言也可能意味不多。显然，它们意味着某种东西，否则就不会被记住、记录或编造出来，但这些说法对当事人的身份究竟有多大分量，可能和现代学者的理解很不一样。想想人名的意义。拜占庭历史上的显赫人物，只要冠有一个在亚美尼亚常见的名字，或一个可以被词源学解释为某个亚美尼亚名字的仿译、翻译乃至变形的名字，就常常——有时甚至总是——被贴上亚美尼亚人的标签，由此产生一些极其牵强的关联，而这些关联之所以能被一本正经地提出，只是因为学界早已习惯了这一谬误所依据的不合逻辑的想法。这种“以名定族”的方法论一直延续，尽管它已被正确地认定为有问题。

诸如巴尔达斯和巴尔达尼斯这样的亚美尼亚名字在罗马社会内部既流行又时髦，正如日耳曼名字在四至六世纪曾风靡一时，且原因大体相同：随着亚美尼亚贵族占据军事和政治领导职位，罗马人也逐渐把这些名字视为有身份的人所用的名字。这在早先的罗马传统中也发生过，涉及伊特鲁里亚、奥斯坎、希腊及其他名字。公元前56年的执政官卢基乌斯·马尔基乌斯·菲利普斯并不是个“希腊人”。名叫米海尔和约翰的皇帝并不是犹太人。马萨诸塞州和俄亥俄州并不比纽约州和宾夕法尼亚州更“印第安”，而约翰·F·肯尼迪也不是个爱尔兰人。

en: Mixed marriages, such as that of Maria the Younger, disseminated common Armenian names further, regardless of the culture or ethnicity of their bearers. Besides, there is a curious double standard at work, in that those specific names were actually of Iranian origin, but no one proposes that their Byzantine bearers were “really” Persians.
By contrast, rarer names such as Mosele and Artabasdos may be more reliable indicators of an Armenian ancestry, though not of an Armenian identity in the present.

The basic problem with this entire approach is that the presumed etymology of one’s name has little or no bearing on one’s ethnicity. Consider the tenth-century Roman legal historian Symbatios. It is convention in the field for this name to mark one as an Armenian (Smbat), but Symbatios, who takes obvious pride in the Roman ethnonym and stresses the lines of continuity between his culture and ancient Rome, “would have thought of himself as no less Roman—despite the Hellenized form of his Armenian name—than Cicero or Julius Caesar.”
zh: 通婚——例如小圣玛丽亚的婚姻——进一步传播了常见的亚美尼亚名字，无论取这些名字的人的文化或族群为何。此外，这里还有一种奇怪的双重标准在起作用：那些特定的名字实际上源自伊朗，却没有人主张拜占庭时期用这些名字的人“其实”是波斯人。
相比之下，莫塞莱和阿尔塔巴斯多斯这类较罕见的名字，或许是亚美尼亚血统更可靠的指标，尽管不是当下亚美尼亚认同的指标。
这整套方法的根本问题在于，一个人的名字据推测有何词源，和这个人的族群身份几无关联。想想十世纪的罗马法律史家辛巴提奥斯。按学界惯例，这个名字标志着一个人是亚美尼亚人（斯姆巴特，Smbat），但辛巴提奥斯明显以罗马族名为荣，并强调他的文化与古罗马之间的连续性脉络，他“会认为自己的罗马性丝毫不亚于西塞罗或尤利乌斯·凯撒——尽管他的亚美尼亚名字采用了希腊化形式”。

en: In practice, the Armenian fallacy is more tenuous than this onomastic error. It would be one thing if we had a network of allied individuals at the court

of whom had “Armenian” names. That might even be interesting. What we actually find is different. I will expose these problems by scrutinizing Signes Codoñer’s recent book on the emperor Theophilos. It is an excellent book that clears up many problems concerning the reign, and I have relied on it and cited it frequently in the present study. One part of it, however, is unpersuasive, namely the proposal that Theophilos’ court was dominated by an Armenian faction that acted in explicit awareness of its ethnicity.
This is a fiction, and typical of much of the scholarship. Let us see how it is constructed.
zh: 在实践中，亚美尼亚谬误赖以成立的依据比以名定族还要薄弱。如果我们面对的是宫廷里有一群彼此结盟的人，他们
都冠有“亚美尼亚”名字，那倒是一回事。那甚至可能颇有意思。但我们实际发现的并非如此。可以拿西格内斯·科多涅尔新近论述狄奥斐卢斯皇帝的著作来看这些问题。这是一部出色的著作，澄清了有关该朝的许多问题，我在本研究中多次依赖并引用它。然而书中有一部分缺乏说服力，即这样一种主张：狄奥斐卢斯的宫廷被一个亚美尼亚派系所主导，这些人明确以本族身份结成派系并采取行动。
这是虚构，也是许多学术研究的典型。让我们看看它是如何被建构起来的。

en: The leader of the Iconoclasts at the court of Theophilos was the patriarch Ioannes the Grammarian, a man vilified and cast as a wizard in Iconophile texts, though he is also presented as a formidable figure. Theophanes Continuatus says this explicitly about him: “He was not a foreigner or a recent arrival, but a true native offspring of this Queen of Cities . . . nor did he come from a humble family, but from one that was quite noble, called Morocharzanioi.”

The name of this family provides no clues as to ethnicity. Based on the rest of this testimony (in a hostile source, no less) it would seem a hopeless task to try and make Ioannes into “an Armenian,” far less into “the leader of the ‘Armenian’ party.” But this is exactly what Signes Codoñer does, by pointing to the alleged names of his father and brother (Pankratios and Arsaber respectively): “This links the family with the Armenian Bagratids.”
No, it doesn’t. Even if the name of his father is accurately reported, Pankratioi are attested in Roman service already in the sixth century,

and the source that reports his father’s name is clearly trying to link the warlock-patriarch to a famous astrologer of the eighth century with the same name; in fact, the name “Pankrates” was a professional name taken by a number of magicians in antiquity.

No source calls Ioannes an Armenian, gives him an Armenian ancestry, or claims that he consorted with Armenians, even though that would have been a convenient way to portray him as a sinister outsider in the polemic that was later directed against him by Iconophiles, as was done with Leon V. This is almost proof that the patriarch was not regarded in Byzantine society as an Armenian. Incidentally, his cousin was Leon the Philosopher, a major thinker of the ninth century. Signes Codoñer is reluctant to Armenianize him too but another scholar confidently makes that connection, on the premise that the cousin of anyone whose father had an Armenian-sounding name must also have been “an Armenian.”
zh: 狄奥斐卢斯宫廷中圣像破坏者的领袖是语法学家约安尼斯牧首，此人在圣像拥护者的文本中被诋毁、被塑造成一个巫师，尽管他也被呈现为一个令人生畏的人物。《狄奥法尼斯续编》（Theophanes Continuatus）明确这样说他：“他不是异邦人，也不是新来者，而是生于斯、长于斯，是这座众城之女皇的子民……他也不是出身寒门，而是出自一个相当高贵的家族，名叫莫罗哈尔扎尼奥伊。”
这个家族的名字没有提供任何族群线索。根据这一证词的其余部分（而且出自一部敌意史料），试图把约安尼斯说成“一个亚美尼亚人”似乎是一项无望的任务，更不用说把他塑造成“‘亚美尼亚’党的领袖”了。但这恰恰是西格内斯·科多涅尔所做的，他拿约安尼斯父亲和兄弟据说使用的名字为据（分别为潘克拉提奥斯和阿尔萨贝尔）：“这就把这个家族与亚美尼亚的巴格拉提德王朝联系起来了。”
不，并没有。即便他父亲的名字被准确报道，早在六世纪，就有名叫潘克拉提奥斯的人在罗马任职，
而且报道他父亲名字的那部史料显然是在试图把这位术士牧首与八世纪一位同名的著名占星家联系起来；事实上，“潘克拉特斯”这个名字是古代若干术士采用的职业名。

没有任何史料称约安尼斯为亚美尼亚人、给他安上亚美尼亚血统，或声称他与亚美尼亚人过从甚密，尽管那本会是在后来圣像拥护者针对他的论战中把他描绘成一个阴险外人的便利方式——就像对利奥五世所做的那样。这几乎证明，这位牧首在拜占庭社会中并不被视为亚美尼亚人。顺带一提，他的表兄弟是哲学家利奥，九世纪的一位重要思想家。西格内斯·科多涅尔并不愿把他也说成亚美尼亚人，但另一位学者却自信地建立了那种联系，其前提是：任何父亲冠有听起来像亚美尼亚名字的人，其表兄弟也必定是“一个亚美尼亚人”。

en: Signes Codoñer also postulates that “it was important for [Theophilos] to give some satisfaction to the Armenian supporters of his inner group . . . with an ‘Armenian’ wedding.”

The marriage to his “Armenian” empress Theodora was arranged either by Theophilos’ (probable) mother Thekla or by his father Michael II’s second wife Euphrosyne, both of whom Signes Codoñer labels as Armenians. However, no source calls any of these women Armenians or sees them as agents of an Armenian faction, so we must scrutinize the basis for these claims. Signes Codoñer identifies Thekla as an Armenian because she was
the daughter of Bardanes the Turk, a leading general of the time and, apparently, also one of the “leading Armenians” of the time.

However, there is no evidence at all that he was an Armenian. All the sources consistently report that Bardanes was called “the Turk,” whatever that meant. Yet because of his personal name, his ethnic moniker is disregarded and he is reclassified as an Armenian, and his alleged daughter along with him (because—remember—if any of your ancestors is an Armenian, you too are “an Armenian”). All this is fiction.
zh: 西格内斯·科多涅尔还推测，“［狄奥斐卢斯］有必要让亲信中的亚美尼亚支持者得到一定的满足……为此举行一场‘亚美尼亚’婚礼。”
他与“亚美尼亚”皇后狄奥多拉的婚姻，要么是由很可能是狄奥斐卢斯之母的特克拉安排的，要么是由他父亲米海尔二世的第二任妻子欧弗罗叙涅安排的，而西格内斯·科多涅尔把这两位都贴上亚美尼亚人的标签。然而，没有任何史料称这些女性中的任何一位为亚美尼亚人，或把她们视为亚美尼亚派系的代理人，因此我们必须审视这些主张的依据。西格内斯·科多涅尔认定特克拉是亚美尼亚人，因为她
是突厥人巴尔达尼斯的女儿——后者是当时的一位主要将领，按这种说法显然也是当时“最有势力的亚美尼亚人”之一。
然而，根本没有证据表明他是亚美尼亚人。所有史料都一贯报道巴尔达尼斯被称为“突厥人”，无论那意味着什么。然而由于他的个人名字，他的“突厥人”这个绰号反被撇在一边，他被重新归类为亚美尼亚人，他据称的女儿也随之被归类（因为——记住——如果你的任何一位祖先是亚美尼亚人，你也是“一个亚美尼亚人”）。这一切都是虚构。

en: What about Euphrosyne, the daughter of Konstantinos VI and second wife of Michael II? She, Signes Codoñer claims, “was also of Armenian blood, for her mother Maria of Amnia came from a Paphlagonian family of Armenian descent.”

Note, however, that Maria of Amnia had married Leon IV (775–780), who was not an Armenian, and that Euphrosyne herself had been raised at the court as a princess of the Romans; therefore, she can have been an Armenian only through a distant relation of “blood,” but this is sufficient for the fallacy to kick in. Yet what proof is there that Maria of Amnia’s Paphlagonian family was “of Armenian descent?” The chronicler Theophanes reports that Maria was brought to the court from the Armeniakoi region, but this refers to the Roman theme of that name, not to her ethnicity.
Maria’s family is known to us through the

children: Life of Saint Philaretos the Merciful,

en: a saintly romance about her father, which does not, however, claim that the family was Armenian; it says only that they lived in the territory throughout which the court sent its men to find a royal bride, namely “the land of the Romans.”

However, Maria had a cousin named Bardas, which is apparently enough to label her entire extended family as Armenian, including her daughter Euphrosyne, even though she was raised at court. As it happens, the

itemizes the names of everyone in Maria’s family, and they are: Philaretos, Ioannes, Hypatia, Euanthia, Myranthia, Petronas, Anthis, Niketas, Petros, Kosmou, Michael, Eirene, Bardas, Eustathios, Helene, and Euphemia. This is a veritable garden of classical Greek and Christian names, but a single Bardas, who is not even here called an Armenian, apparently trumps all the rest in the logic of the fallacy.
And that is the entire basis for the claim that Euphrosyne was “of Armenian blood.”
zh: 那么欧弗罗叙涅呢？她是君士坦丁六世的女儿、米海尔二世的第二任妻子。西格内斯·科多涅尔声称，她“也有亚美尼亚血统，因为她的母亲阿姆尼亚的玛丽亚出自一个亚美尼亚裔的帕夫拉戈尼亚家族”。
然而请注意，阿姆尼亚的玛丽亚嫁给了君士坦丁六世，后者不是亚美尼亚人，而欧弗罗叙涅本人是在宫廷中作为罗马人的公主被抚养长大的；因此，她只能通过一种遥远的“血”缘关系才可能是亚美尼亚人，但这就足以让人套用上述谬误。然而，有什么证据表明阿姆尼亚的玛丽亚的帕夫拉戈尼亚家族是“亚美尼亚裔”呢？编年史家狄奥法尼斯报道，玛丽亚是从亚美尼亚军区被带到宫廷的，但这指的是那个名字的罗马军区，而非她的族群性。
我们通过《仁慈者圣菲拉雷托斯传》（Life of Saint Philaretos the Merciful）得知玛丽亚的家族，这是一部关于她外祖父的圣徒传奇，其中并未声称这个家族是亚美尼亚人；它只说他们住在宫廷派人四处寻找皇家新娘的那片土地上，即“罗马人的土地”。

然而，玛丽亚有一个名叫巴尔达斯的表兄弟，这显然就足以把她的整个大家庭贴上亚美尼亚标签，包括她的女儿欧弗罗叙涅，尽管后者是在宫廷长大的。碰巧，该《传》逐一列出了玛丽亚家族中每个人的名字，它们是：菲拉雷托斯、约安尼斯、希帕提娅、欧安提娅、米兰提娅、佩特罗纳、安提斯、尼基塔斯、彼得罗斯、科斯穆、米海尔、伊琳娜、巴尔达斯、欧斯塔提奥斯、海伦妮和欧菲米娅。这简直是满眼都是古典希腊和基督教的名字，但一个巴尔达斯——他在这里甚至没有被称为亚美尼亚人——在谬误的逻辑中显然压倒了其余所有名字。
而这就是声称欧弗罗叙涅“有亚美尼亚血统”的全部依据。

en: What, then, about Theodora, whose marriage to Theophilos was supposed to appease the (alleged) Armenian faction? As the restorer of icons in 843, many texts discuss her, yet none refers to her Armenian ethnicity. As we have seen, for example regarding Maria of Vizye, Konstantinos (the ancestor of Genesios), and Alexios Mosele, an Armenian ancestry was the sort of thing that Byzantine sources could mention without harming the reputations of their subjects; it was not something that had to be hidden. But they say nothing of the sort regarding Theodora. So what is the claim based on? She was from the province of Paphlagonia and her parents were named Marinos and Theoktiste Florina. Signes Codoñer lamely suggests that the name Marinos may have been popular among Armenians, but the key pieces of evidence are, first, that her brother was named Bardas—a name treated like a DNA marker of Armenian ethnicity. Yet her other siblings were named Petronas, Sophia, Maria, and Eirene. This gets us nowhere. The second piece of evidence is that her uncle Manuel—apparently paternal—is in fact said in the sources to have been an Armenian or, rather, “descended from the Armenians.”
Signes Codoñer concludes that this “confirmed the Armenian descent of her family.”

But why? Surely we can imagine a number of scenarios that could have included an uncle “descended from the Armenians” (which, as we have seen, still does not mean that he “was” an Armenian). It is significant that the sources make this claim about him only and not about any other member of this well-documented family; they especially do not make this claim about his niece, the empress Theodora. This is true not only in the Roman sources. The thirteenth-century Armenian historical compiler Vardan explicitly calls Manuel a Mamikonian (a leading Armenian clan), but not Theodora or any other member of her family.
zh: 那么狄奥多拉呢？她与狄奥斐卢斯的婚姻本应安抚那个（据称的）亚美尼亚派系。她在843年恢复了圣像崇拜，许多文献都提到她，却没有一部提到她的亚美尼亚族群性。正如我们所见，例如关于维济耶的玛丽亚、君士坦丁（格内西奥斯的祖先）和阿莱克修斯·莫塞莱，亚美尼亚血统是拜占庭史料可以提及而不损害其传主声誉的那类事情；它不是必须隐瞒的东西。但关于狄奥多拉，它们只字未提这类事情。那么这一主张基于什么？她来自帕夫拉戈尼亚行省，父母名叫马里诺斯和塞奥克提斯特·弗洛里娜。西格内斯·科多涅尔勉强提出，马里诺斯这个名字可能在亚美尼亚人中流行，但关键的证据首先是：她的兄弟名叫巴尔达斯——一个被当作亚美尼亚族群性DNA标记的名字。然而她的其他兄弟姐妹名叫佩特罗纳、索菲娅、玛丽亚和伊琳娜。这毫无助益。第二条证据是，她的叔父曼努埃尔（看来是她父亲的兄弟）事实上在史料中被说成是亚美尼亚人，或者更确切地说，“是亚美尼亚人的后裔”。
西格内斯·科多涅尔断定，这“证实了她家族的亚美尼亚血统”。

但为什么呢？我们当然能设想若干可能包含一位“亚美尼亚人后裔”叔父的情形（正如我们所见，这仍不意味着他“就是”亚美尼亚人）。重要的是，这个家族在史料中记载甚详，却只有他一人被说成是亚美尼亚人的后裔；它们尤其不对他的侄女、皇后狄奥多拉作出这一声称。这不仅适用于罗马史料。十三世纪的亚美尼亚历史编纂者瓦尔丹明确称曼努埃尔为马米科尼扬家族成员（一个首要的亚美尼亚氏族），却不这样称狄奥多拉或她家族的任何其他成员。

en: The preceding discussion of Theophilos’ wider family has exposed the strained logic and fictions that the Armenian fallacy requires, and it undermines the theory that his court was “controlled by Armenians.”

Two of its prominent members, Alexios Mosele and Manuel, are said to have had Armenian ancestry, but even this does not necessarily mean that they were less Roman than the rest of the court. There is also no proof that they based their actions on their ethnicity (when Manuel had to flee the court at one point he went not to Armenia but to the caliphate). Interestingly, Signes Codoñer often places the words “Roman” and “Romanized” in scare quotes while treating “Armenian” straightforwardly, as if it did not require similar skepticism.

It would be more accurate to do the exact opposite. It is the Armenian claims that are made on behalf of Roman generals in the sources that must be treated as deliberate strategies of distinction among the Roman military elite. At one point, Signes Codoñer correctly warns that “we must be very careful with these genealogies, used by individuals for particular purposes but not necessarily reflecting any real ancestry.”
Unfortunately, his own methodology ignores this warning.
zh: 前面对狄奥斐卢斯大家族的讨论，揭示了这种谬误赖以成立的牵强逻辑与虚构，也动摇了他的宫廷“被亚美尼亚人控制”的理论。
其中两位显赫成员阿莱克修斯·莫塞莱和曼努埃尔据称有亚美尼亚血统，但即便如此，也不一定意味着他们没有宫廷中的其他人那么罗马化。也没有证据表明他们以族群性为行事依据（曼努埃尔有一次不得不逃离宫廷时，他去的不是亚美尼亚，而是哈里发国）。有意思的是，西格内斯·科多涅尔常常给“罗马”和“罗马化”这两个词加上警示引号，却直截了当地对待“亚美尼亚”，仿佛它不需要类似的怀疑。
恰恰相反的做法会更准确。真正需要审慎看待的，是史料中关于罗马将领有亚美尼亚出身的说法。这类说法有其用意，让他们在罗马军中其他显贵之间显得与众不同。西格内斯·科多涅尔在一处正确地警告说，“我们必须对这些家系非常小心，它们被个人用于特定目的，却不一定反映任何真实的血统”。
遗憾的是，他自己的方法论无视了这一警告。

en: The Armenian fallacy is pervasive, and I have focused on this one book because it is recent (2014), offers an otherwise excellent reconstruction of a reign, exhibits many of the far-fetched connections and associations that are often used to convert Romans into Armenians, and uses them to build up to a big thesis about the power of “Armenians” at the court. The next step is to postulate that these Armenians behaved in ethnic solidarity: if two men “were of Armenian origin, some kind of special relationship between them is to be presupposed,” and “Armenian elites favored marriage among [their] countrymen.”

But there is no proof for either notion that does not rest on the fallacy. Moreover, it is risky (or worse) to believe that people will “band together” and form a faction based on common ancestry. Armenians were just as divided among themselves.
zh: 亚美尼亚谬误无处不在，我之所以聚焦于这一本书，是因为它新近出版（2014），在其他方面出色地重建了狄奥斐卢斯一朝的历史，展示了常被用来把罗马人变成亚美尼亚人的许多牵强联系与关联，并用它们逐步构建起一个关于“亚美尼亚人”在宫廷中权势的总论。下一步是设定这些亚美尼亚人以族群团结的方式行事：如果两个人“是亚美尼亚起源，就必须预设他们之间存在某种特殊关系”，而且“亚美尼亚精英偏好在［他们的］同胞之间通婚”。
然而，若不靠上述谬误，这两种说法就都没有证据。此外，相信人们会基于共同血统“抱团”并形成派系，是冒险的（甚至更糟）。亚美尼亚人内部同样四分五裂。

en: It has become customary for scholars of Byzantium to attach Armenian ethnic labels to Roman families whose history unfolded entirely within the empire and never in Armenia. This type of racialized thinking is widespread and mainstream. A vigorous debate has taken place on whether such and such a family did or did not have an Armenian ancestry, but rarely is it asked why that one strand of ancestry is treated with such exceptional attention, especially when the families in question and the sources about them made no such claims to an Armenian ancestry. If they did make such a claim, we should ask what it meant in its Roman context. If they did not, and the sources did not either, we should wonder why we deem it so important to make them ourselves. The grounds on which these ethnic origins are alleged are often extremely tenuous, and this whole way of thinking rests on the assumption that “families” have aboriginal ethnicities that in some unexplained way define them forever after.
zh: 拜占庭学者们已经习惯于给那些历史完全在帝国境内展开、从未在亚美尼亚展开的罗马家族贴上亚美尼亚族群标签。这种种族化的思维广泛存在且属主流。围绕某某家族究竟有没有亚美尼亚血统，已经发生过激烈的辩论，却很少有人问：为什么那一支血统受到如此格外的关注，尤其当涉事家族及关于它们的史料都未曾作出亚美尼亚血统的声称时。如果它们确实作出了这样的声称，我们应当问它在罗马语境中意味着什么。如果它们没有，史料也没有，我们就应当纳闷，为什么我们自己觉得作出这种声称如此重要。提出这些族群出身说法的依据往往极其薄弱，而这整套思维方式都基于一个假设：“家族”拥有某种与生俱来的族群身份，可以永远界定整个家族，至于为什么能如此，这套思路却说不清。

en: In the absence of firm historical evidence for ethnic claims, aboriginal ethnicities are modern fictions and so debates over them have an unreal quality. Moreover, recent scholarship has “appreciably reduced [the] more enthusiastic earlier estimates” by Adontz and Charanis regarding the number of Roman families of Armenian descent.
The families of Phokas, Dalassenos, Bourtzes, and Doukas have been removed from that list, on which they had been placed originally for the same flimsy (i.e., nonexistent) reasons.

Yet we may be skeptical of many who have survived this winnowing process too, for example the Lakapenos, Kourkouas, and Skleros families, whom Byzantinists routinely call “Armenians.” Let us look at them.
zh: 在缺乏族群声称的坚实历史证据的情况下，所谓家族固有的族群身份只是现代人的虚构，围绕它们的辩论也失了依托。此外，晚近研究已经“大幅缩减了阿东茨和查拉尼斯就亚美尼亚裔罗马家族数量所作的［那些］更热情的早期估计”。
福卡斯、达拉塞努斯、布尔茨斯和杜卡斯这些家族已被从那份名单上移除，而它们最初正是出于同样站不住脚的（即不存在的）理由被列上去的。
然而，对许多筛选后仍留在名单上的家族，我们也可能持怀疑态度，例如拉卡佩努斯、库尔库阿斯和斯克莱罗斯家族，拜占庭学家们惯常称它们为“亚美尼亚人”。让我们看看它们。

en: Romanos I Lakapenos (920–944) is discussed in many Roman sources, but none of them calls him an Armenian. His father was Theophylaktos Abastaktos, who is also not called an Armenian in the single report that we have about him (but because Romanos was of humble origin and is assumed to have been “of Armenian descent,” his father has retroactively been reclassified as “an Armenian peasant”).
However, Liudprand, the bishop of Cremona in Italy who visited Constantinople after Romanos’ reign, does report that Romanos was “of humble origin and of the Armenian people.”

This is odd. Why would no Byzantine source mention this, but we find it instead in a Latin text written by a foreigner? Fortunately, this is easy to explain. Romanos came from the village of Lakapa, which the Romans situated in the theme of Armeniakon (broadly defined). For example, Romanos found a wife for the brother of the Bulgarian tsar, and she was a woman from Romanos’ “own homeland in the Armeniakon (Ἀρμενιακῶν) theme.”

It would be easy for a Latin writer such as Liudprand to muddle the distinction between an Armenios (an Armenian) and an Armeniakos (a resident of the Roman theme of the Armeniakoi), especially as the Byzantines, following ancient conventions, could refer to people from a specific province of the empire as having their
or
there. One could be “an Armeniakos by
” or “from a
of the Armeniakon.”
These labels were not ethnicities, but designations of a specific provincial origin. It could be said of a woman that she “drew her
from the Opsikion,” that is, the theme of that name. No modern scholar has postulated an Opsikian ethnicity on that basis.
Likewise, one’s
could be from the province Boukellarioi,
or, as here, from the Armeniakoi.
zh: 罗曼努斯一世·拉卡佩努斯（920–944）见于许多罗马史料，但没有一部称他为亚美尼亚人。他的父亲是塞奥菲拉克托斯·阿巴斯塔克托斯，在我们关于他的唯一一则报道中，他也没有被称为亚美尼亚人（但由于罗曼努斯出身寒微，且被假定为“亚美尼亚裔”，他的父亲已被追溯性地重新归类为“一个亚美尼亚农民”）。
然而，意大利克雷莫纳主教利乌特普兰德——他在罗曼努斯朝之后访问过君士坦丁堡——确实报道罗曼努斯“出身寒微，属亚美尼亚人民”。
这很奇怪。为什么没有拜占庭史料提到这一点，我们却在一部由异邦人撰写的拉丁文本中发现了它？幸运的是，这很容易解释。罗曼努斯来自拉卡帕村，罗马人认为该村属于广义的亚美尼亚军区。例如，罗曼努斯为保加尔沙皇的兄弟找了一位妻子，她就是来自罗曼努斯“自己在亚美尼亚军区（Ἀρμενιακῶν）的故土”的女子。
对利乌特普兰德这样的拉丁作者来说，很容易把 Armenios（亚美尼亚人）和 Armeniakos（罗马亚美尼亚军区居民）混为一谈，尤其因为拜占庭人沿袭古代惯例，可以把来自帝国某个特定行省的人说成其族类（genos）或故土（patris）在那里。一个人可以是“按族类（genos）而言的亚美尼亚军区人”，或“出自亚美尼亚军区的族类（genos）”。
这些称谓说明某人出身于哪个行省。可以说某个女子“她的族类（genos）来自奥普西基翁”，即那个名字的军区。从没有现代学者仅凭这话便假定存在一个奥普西基翁族群。
同样，一个人的族类（genos）可以来自布凯拉里奥伊行省，
或者如此处一样，来自亚美尼亚军区。

en: If Lakapa has been correctly identified—of which I am not certain—it lay between Kaisareia and Melitene in eastern Cappadocia.

In 908, this region was incorporated into the theme of Lykandos founded by Melias (Mleh), an (actual and so-called) Armenian in Roman service. The theme was subsequently settled by Armenians, but this happened long after Romanos I’s association with the place, whatever exactly it was (he was born around 870). We are explicitly told that when Melias was authorized to create this frontier theme, “he found the land empty and uninhabited.”

So we should not project its later (mostly Armenian) demography onto the ninth century, when the territory belonged to the wider orbit of the Armeniakon theme. In fact, there is a good reason to doubt that Romanos’ origins in Lakapa (assuming he was from there) had anything to do with his ethnicity. The one thing that we know about his father Abastaktos is that he saved the life of the emperor Basileios I in battle, in 871. Offered a reward, Abastaktos refused offices and titles and asked instead for a
which in context probably means imperial land on which to settle.

Basileios I was just then creating new themes in the east, specifically the theme Charsianon, which was founded between 863 and 872 in territory detached from Armeniakon that included the future Lykandos.
It is therefore likely that Romanos was from Lakapa because his father settled there in an earlier phase of Roman expansion in the region.
zh: 如果拉卡帕已被正确认定——对此我并不确定——它位于卡帕多基亚东部的凯撒利亚与梅利泰内之间。
908年，这一地区被并入由梅利亚斯（姆莱赫）创建的利坎多斯军区，梅利亚斯确实是亚美尼亚人，史料也这样称呼他，当时在罗马任职。后来才有亚美尼亚人迁到该军区定居，但这发生在罗曼努斯一世与该地产生关联之后很久，无论那关联究竟是什么（他约生于870年）。我们被明确告知，当梅利亚斯获准创建这个边境军区时，“他发现那片土地空着，无人定居”。

因此我们不应把它后来（以亚美尼亚人为主）的人口结构投射到九世纪，当时这片领土属于亚美尼亚军区更广泛的范围。事实上，有充分理由怀疑罗曼努斯在拉卡帕的起源（假定他来自那里）与他的族群性有任何关系。关于他父亲阿巴斯塔克托斯，我们所知的一件事是，他在871年的一场战斗中救了瓦西里一世皇帝的命。皇帝要奖赏他时，阿巴斯塔克托斯拒绝了官职和头衔，转而请求一块皇家土地（topos basilikos），在语境中这大概指可供他定居的帝国土地。
瓦西里一世当时正在东部创建新军区，特别是哈尔西亚农军区，它于863至872年间在从亚美尼亚军区分离出来的领土上建立，那片领土包括了未来的利坎多斯。
因此，罗曼努斯之所以来自拉卡帕，很可能是因为他父亲在罗马向该地区扩张的较早阶段就在那里定居了。

en: Romanos was not “an Armenian.” But his alleged ethnicity has been repeated so often in the literature that it has acquired the status of a known fact, even though it is based on the most tenuous of indirect connections. It is therefore all the more important that we not use his alleged origins to explain his policies, as has also been done,

especially when we can explain those policies just as well without it. Even if he had (some) Armenian ancestry, we still should not use it to explain his actions. Ancestry is not destiny. That belief is what today we call “racism.” It is also a mistaken way of explaining people’s actions.
zh: 罗曼努斯不是“一个亚美尼亚人”。但他据称的族群性在文献中被重复了太多次，以至于获得了已知事实的地位，尽管它建立在最薄弱的间接联系之上。因此，我们尤其不应像已经有人做的那样，用他据称的起源来解释他的政策，
特别是当我们不用它也能同样好地解释那些政策时。即便他有（某种）亚美尼亚血统，我们仍不应用它来解释他的行为。血统不是命运。那种信念就是我们今天所称的“种族主义”。它也是解释人们行为的一种错误方式。

en: A word of clarification must be said here about the Armeniakon theme and its population. Historians often conclude from its name that its population must have been predominantly Armenian, but this inference can be conclusively refuted. The name of this middle Byzantine theme derives from the name of the field army established much farther to the east in 528 by Justinian to operate in Armenia. The general in command of this army held the title

children: magister militum per Armeniam et Pontum Polemoniacum et gentes.

en: When that army was pulled back to Asia Minor during the defeats of the seventh century, it gave its name to the huge new province of Armeniakon (the same happened with other provinces in Asia Minor into which the other field armies were withdrawn).
zh: 这里还需说明亚美尼亚军区及其人口的情况。史家们常常从它的名字推断其人口必定以亚美尼亚人为主，但这一推断可以被确凿地驳倒。这个中期拜占庭军区的名字，源自查士丁尼于528年在更偏东的地方为亚美尼亚战事组建的那支野战军的名字。统率这支军队的将军拥有“亚美尼亚、本都波勒莫尼亚库斯及诸族方面军统帅”（magister militum per Armeniam et Pontum Polemoniacum et gentes）的头衔。当那支军队在七世纪的败绩中被撤回到小亚细亚时，新设的亚美尼亚军区幅员辽阔，其名称就沿自这支部队（其他野战军被撤入的小亚细亚其他行省也发生了同样的情况）。

en: Neither the original field army created by Justinian nor its descendant thematic army in Asia Minor was named after the ethnic origin of their soldiers, though this error is sometimes asserted.
Justinian’s edict instituting the army
survives along with narrative sources about the event, and they all say that the new army was made up of Roman soldiers who were transferred there from Roman armies elsewhere. They were

meant to replace the inadequate units of local Armenians used by the governors of Roman Armenia down to that point, in order to “make the Roman army less dependent militarily on local levies and the armed retinues of members of the indigenous Armenian aristocracy.”
It is possible that over time that army did recruit soldiers locally, but that is not where its name came from. The name came from its being stationed
Armenia.
zh: 无论是查士丁尼创建的原初野战军，还是后来在小亚细亚的军区部队，都不是以其士兵的族群起源命名的，尽管这一错误有时被断言。
查士丁尼设立亚美尼亚方面军（per Armeniam）的敕令，与关于此事的叙事史料一同存世，它们都说这支新军由从罗马驻其他地方的军队调来的士兵组成。他们
是为了取代罗马亚美尼亚总督们此前一直使用的、由当地亚美尼亚人组成的不敷使用的部队，以便“使罗马军队在军事上更少依赖地方征召兵和当地亚美尼亚贵族的武装扈从”。
随着时间推移，那支军队有可能确实在当地招募士兵，但它的名字并非由此而来。这个名字源于它驻扎
亚美尼亚。

en: When the army retreated from Armenia proper into Asia Minor, it kept its name even though it was now stationed in Roman territories whose population contained a smaller Armenian element (as we will see in Chapter 6). The names of Roman provinces are no sure indication of their ethnic makeup. This is certainly the case with Armeniakon, whose name stems from a Roman army that was created to operate in Armenia but was then pulled back into Asia Minor. But the names of other provinces along the frontier sometimes gestured to what lay beyond them, for example the late Roman Balkan province of Scythia (which was not inhabited by Scythians), the theme of Longobardia (in Apulia), the command of Iberia (which contained only a small part of Georgia, Kartli), and the theme of Mesopotamia. We can perhaps think of the relationship between Armeniakon and Armenia as that between the U.S. state of New Mexico and the adjacent country of Mexico. Many Mexicans live in New Mexico along with American citizens of Mexican origin, but most of the population is neither.
zh: 当这支军队从亚美尼亚本土撤入小亚细亚时，它保留了自己的名字，尽管它如今驻扎在罗马领土上，当地居民中的亚美尼亚人已没有那么多（正如我们将在第6章看到的）。罗马行省的名字并不是其族群构成的可靠指示。亚美尼亚军区无疑如此，它的名字源自一支为在亚美尼亚作战而创建、随后被撤回小亚细亚的罗马军队。但还有一些边境行省，其名称指的是边境另一侧的地区，例如晚期罗马的巴尔干行省斯基提亚（那里并不住着斯基泰人）、伦巴第军区（在阿普利亚）、伊比利亚督军区（只包含格鲁吉亚的一小部分，即卡特利）和美索不达米亚军区。我们或许可以把亚美尼亚军区与亚美尼亚的关系，想成美国新墨西哥州与邻国墨西哥的关系。许多墨西哥人与墨西哥裔美国公民一起住在新墨西哥，但人口的大多数两者都不是。

en: Our imperial geographer Konstantinos VII says that Armeniakon took its name from the Armenian people who lived “adjacent to its border” and that the theme was located “in proximity to them,” which is true because Justinian’s field army was stationed in Armenia, to the east of the later Armeniakon theme. Konstantinos adds that parts of the theme by Koloneia, that is, the easternmost parts, were inhabited by Armenians.

This is significant: Konstantinos VII could distinguish between Armenians and Romans living in the theme of Armeniakon, and the former were in his view a majority in only one small region. Therefore, we should not automatically assume that a person from Armeniakon was also an Armenian. Charanis claimed that the thematic army of Armeniakon “consisted primarily of Armenians,” but the passage of Theophanes that he cites as proof demonstrates instead that the “Armenians” were a separate unit from the regular army of the Armeniakon theme, thus directly undercutting his argument.
( This sort of confusion could be avoided if scholars were willing to place Byzantium in its larger Roman context. No historian of the later Republic would argue that the
was composed of Germans.)
zh: 我们的帝国地理学家君士坦丁七世说，亚美尼亚军区得名于居于“边界外紧邻之处”的亚美尼亚人，军区地处“与他们相近”之处。这个说法有其道理，因为查士丁尼的野战军驻扎在亚美尼亚，在后来亚美尼亚军区的东边。君士坦丁补充说，该军区靠近科洛内亚的部分，即最东边的部分，住着亚美尼亚人。
这很重要：君士坦丁七世能够区分住在亚美尼亚军区的亚美尼亚人与罗马人，而在他看来前者只在一个小地区占多数。因此，我们不应自动假定一个来自亚美尼亚军区的人也是亚美尼亚人。查拉尼斯声称该军区的部队“主要由亚美尼亚人组成”，但他引为证据的那段狄奥法尼斯文字反而表明，“亚美尼亚人”是与亚美尼亚军区正规军分开的一支部队，从而直接削弱了他的论点。
（如果学者们愿意把拜占庭放回更广阔的罗马史中，这种混淆本可避免。没有一位研究后期罗马共和国的史家会主张第一日耳曼军团（Legio I Germanica）是由日耳曼人组成的。）

en: Roman writers were usually consistent in distinguishing between ethnic Armenians and the inhabitants and soldiers of the Armeniakon theme, even when the two overlapped.
Consider the case of “Artabasdos, an Armenian and the general of the Armeniakoi.”

Sometimes there was slippage between the two concepts, or scribal errors in copying these two words that looked similar, but this does not affect the case of Romanos I Lakapenos. There are also modern scholars, proponents of the Armenian fallacy, who carelessly write Ἀρμενίων (“of the Armenians”) when the text actually says Ἀρμενιακῶν (“of the Armeniakoi theme”), and thereby produce more fictitious “Armenians.”
At any rate, we can now understand the origin of the misleading report in Liudprand.
zh: 罗马作者一般会明确区分亚美尼亚族人和亚美尼亚军区的居民及士兵，即便两者有所重叠。
想想“阿尔塔巴斯多斯，一个亚美尼亚人兼亚美尼亚军区的将军”这个例子。
有时两个概念的界线会变得模糊，或者抄写这两个看起来相似的词时出现笔误，但这不影响罗曼努斯一世·拉卡佩努斯的例子。还有一些现代学者，即亚美尼亚谬误的拥护者，在文本实际写作 Ἀρμενιακῶν（“亚美尼亚军区的”）时粗心地写成 Ἀρμενίων（“亚美尼亚人的”），从而制造出更多虚构的“亚美尼亚人”。
无论如何，我们现在能够理解利乌特普兰德那则误导性报道的起源了。

en: If we scrutinize the evidence that is cited to prove that other Roman families were “of Armenian descent,” we obtain the same negative results, even if we focus on those cases that have been “chosen very conservatively from families still considered of clear Armenian origin, such as the Skleroi (despite the reservations of Kazhdan), Lakapenoi, Kourkouas-Tzimiskai,” and others.

These are supposed to be the safest examples, but upon inspection they turn out to be flimsy. The Skleros family is often touted as “Armenian,” but the evidence for this claim is just as tenuous as for the Lakapenoi, in fact more so. It consists of one early ninth-century Skleros said by a highly unreliable text (the
) to have come from the Roman province of Armenia Minor (not that he was “an Armenian”), and this figure may or may not have been related to the later family with the same surname.
No source claims that any later Skleros—say, in the later tenth century—was “an Armenian,” though many scholars make that claim.
zh: 如果我们审视被引用来证明其他罗马家族“是亚美尼亚裔”的证据，会得到同样的否定结果，即便我们聚焦于那些“非常保守地从仍被认为有明确亚美尼亚起源的家族中挑选出来的例子，例如斯克莱罗斯家族（尽管卡日丹有所保留）、拉卡佩努斯家族、库尔库阿斯—齐米斯凯斯家族”等等。
这些本应是最稳妥的例子，但一经检视便显得站不住脚。斯克莱罗斯家族常被吹捧为“亚美尼亚的”，但这一声称的证据与拉卡佩努斯家族的一样薄弱，事实上更薄弱。证据只涉及九世纪初一名斯克莱罗斯。据极不可靠的《莫奈姆瓦夏编年史》（Chronicle of Monembasia）所记，他来自罗马的小亚美尼亚行省（并不是说他是“一个亚美尼亚人”），而此人与后来那个同姓的家族有没有亲缘关系，无法确定。
没有任何史料声称任何较晚的斯克莱罗斯——比如十世纪后期的——是“一个亚美尼亚人”，尽管许多学者作出这种声称。

en: Beyond their alleged ancestry, however, what exactly are we saying about otherwise fully Roman figures such as Bardas Skleros and Ioannes Tzimiskes when we call them “Armenians” or “of Armenian descent”? Even if one believes in blood—whatever that means— “after very few generations of intermarriages, such as those between the ‘Iberian’ Phokades and the ‘Armenian’ Skleroi or Kourkouas Tzimiskai . . . the question of
could hardly be raised.”

We must, moreover, remember that this entire discussion is conducted in a realm of modern fantasy, since the original sources, which were capable of mentioning someone’s ethnicity when it was relevant (and even when it was not), say nothing whatever about “Iberian” Phokades or “Armenian” Skleroi. In fact, in the sources “Byzantines of Armenian origin are ethnically identified as to origin more frequently than are Byzantines of any other origin.”
This gives us a presumptive basis to treat silence as absence.
zh: 然而，撇开他们据称的血统，当我们把巴尔达斯·斯克莱罗斯和约安尼斯·齐米斯凯斯这样在其他方面完全罗马的人物称为“亚美尼亚人”或“亚美尼亚裔”时，我们究竟在说什么？即便一个人相信血统——无论那意味着什么——“通婚不过几代之后，例如‘伊比利亚’福卡斯家族与‘亚美尼亚’斯克莱罗斯家族或库尔库阿斯·齐米斯凯斯家族之间的通婚……血统纯洁（limpieza de sangre）的问题几乎无从提起”。
此外，我们必须记住，这整场讨论是在一个现代幻想的领域里进行的，因为原始史料——它们能够在相关时（甚至不相关时）提及某人的族群性——对“伊比利亚”福卡斯家族或“亚美尼亚”斯克莱罗斯家族只字未提。事实上，在史料中，“与其他出身的拜占庭人相比，有亚美尼亚出身的人最常被史料特意点明族群来源”。
因此，史料的沉默可以作为推断这种出身并不存在的依据。

en: Jean-Claude Cheynet correctly observes that “after a few generations nostalgic feelings toward a family’s place of origin could gradually vanish. Nothing indicates that the Skleroi of the eleventh century felt the importance of their Armenian roots, or that the Branades of the twelfth–thirteenth centuries remembered their Slavic origins.” Yet in a footnote he adds: “By contrast, during the tenth century, Bardas Skleros’ revolt was largely supported by Armenians,” the implication being that he was drawn to them (or they to him) on the basis of ethnic affinity.
It is common for historians to postulate ethnic affinities in the case of this war.

Some versions of the Armenian fallacy here outdo themselves, such as the proposal that Armenians may have supported Skleros because they remembered the Armenian blood of the emperor Ioannes Tzimiskes (969– 976), Skleros’ former son-in-law.

Moreover, the fallacy always has to be selective as, according to some of its other incarnations, Skleros’ enemies (the Phokades and the Macedonian dynasty) were also of Armenian descent or Armenians.
Did all this Armenian blood cancel itself out at some point, like Buridan’s ass? If all Byzantines were Armenian, there could not then have been an Armenian faction among them.
zh: 让-克洛德·谢内正确地指出，“几代之后，对一个家族起源之地的怀旧情感可能逐渐消失。没有任何迹象表明十一世纪的斯克莱罗斯家族感到他们亚美尼亚根源的重要性，或十二至十三世纪的布拉纳德斯家族记得他们的斯拉夫起源”。然而他在一条脚注中补充说：“相比之下，在十世纪，巴尔达斯·斯克莱罗斯的叛乱在很大程度上得到了亚美尼亚人的支持”，言外之意是，他是由于族群出身而亲近这些人，或这些人因此亲近他。
史家们在这场战争的事例中设定族群亲和是常有的事。
亚美尼亚谬误的某些版本在这里更是变本加厉，例如这样一种主张：亚美尼亚人可能支持斯克莱罗斯，因为他们记得约安尼斯·齐米斯凯斯皇帝（969–976）的亚美尼亚血统。齐米斯凯斯曾娶斯克莱罗斯的姊妹。
此外，谬误总是不得不有所选择，因为按这种谬误的另外一些说法，斯克莱罗斯的敌人（福卡斯家族和马其顿王朝）也是亚美尼亚裔或亚美尼亚人。
所有这些亚美尼亚血统是否在某个时刻相互抵消了，就像布里丹之驴？如果所有拜占庭人都是亚美尼亚人，那么他们中间就不可能有一个亚美尼亚派系。

en: Skleros did in fact receive support from ethnic Armenian units when he rebelled against Basileios II in 976–979 and again later in 989. But his rebel army was predominantly Roman, and he also sought support from Arabs, Kurds, and others, eventually also the Persian Buyids.

The prominence of Armenians in his army was due to the fact that he raised his rebellion in the southeast, in regions that the empire had militarized in the tenth century through the settlement of Armenian colonists. There is no reason to think that Skleros’ choice of allies had anything to do with ethnic affinity, nor do our sources suggest anything like that. What we have is a rebel general mustering all the support that he could find. Let us keep in mind that Skleros’ “Armenian roots” have not been proven, anyway; that the family has a documented history of imperial service since the early ninth century, almost two hundred years before the rebellion, which is more than just a few generations; and that much of that service took place in the empire’s Balkan provinces. There is no reason to ethnicize Bardas Skleros’ wartime politics.
zh: 斯克莱罗斯在976–979年反叛瓦西里二世、以及后来989年再次反叛时，确实得到了由亚美尼亚族人组成的部队的支持。但他的叛军以罗马人为主，他也寻求阿拉伯人、库尔德人及其他人的支持，后来还求助于波斯的白益王朝。

亚美尼亚人在他军队中的突出地位，是由于他在东南部发动叛乱，而那些地区是帝国在十世纪通过安置亚美尼亚殖民者加强军事部署的。没有理由认为斯克莱罗斯对盟友的选择与族群亲和有任何关系，我们的史料也没有暗示任何这类事情。我们看到的是一位叛乱将军在集结他所能找到的一切支持。让我们记住：斯克莱罗斯的“亚美尼亚根源”无论如何尚未被证实；这个家族自九世纪初以来就有记载详尽的帝国仕途史，比叛乱早了近两百年，这远不止几代人；而且那段仕途的大部分发生在帝国的巴尔干行省。没有理由以族群来解释巴尔达斯·斯克莱罗斯在战时的政治选择。

en: Many more individuals and families have been ethnicized on the basis of such flimsy or inconclusive evidence, their behaviors then explained on the basis of “race” or “blood.” The eleventh-century general Katakalon Kekaumenos—a thoroughly Roman figure—is said in one article to have “still had affinities with his old race,” which of course is Armenian.

It would be otiose to interrogate all such claims. If the reader has not already been convinced that this methodology is flawed, more examples will not make a difference. The preceding analysis will have served its purpose if the reader, forewarned, approaches this racial fallacy in Byzantine Studies with due skepticism.
zh: 还有更多的个人和家族基于这类站不住脚或不确定的证据被归入某个族群，他们的行为随后又基于“种族”或“血统”来解释。十一世纪的将军卡塔卡隆·凯考梅诺斯——一位标准的罗马人——在一篇文章中被说成“仍与他的旧种族有亲和”，而那当然是亚美尼亚。
不必逐条追问所有这类说法。如果读者尚未确信这种方法论有缺陷，更多例子也不会改变什么。只要读者预先得到警示，以应有的怀疑态度对待拜占庭研究中的这种种族谬误，前面的分析就已达到了它的目的。

en: “Armenian” Emperors
zh: “亚美尼亚”皇帝

en: The consensual mass hallucination that is the Armenian fallacy has populated Byzantine history with a series of alleged “Armenian” emperors. A longer list of them (proposed by Adontz) has been winnowed down by later scholars to a few cases that are “self-evident,” including Philippikos Bardanes (711–713), Leon V (813–820), Basileios I (867– 886), Romanos I Lakapenos (920–944), and Ioannes I Tzimiskes (969–976).
As we saw, however, the case of Romanos I Lakapenos is hardly self-evident, and, when we follow the trail of footnotes for

of the rest too, to say nothing of Maurikios (582–602), Herakleios (610–641), or Nikephoros I (802–811), it becomes apparent that these confident assertions are built on sand and have become established only through uncritical repetition. But before we delve into the dubious methodologies by which Armenian emperors have been manufactured, we have again to question what exactly is being asserted. What does it mean to call an emperor an “Armenian” when neither he, his subjects, or any actual Armenians recognized him as such? When no such claim is made about him in the sources? When his language, religion, political affiliation, and cultural profile were all Roman?
zh: 亚美尼亚谬误成了学界共同接受的一种幻觉，让拜占庭史上出现了一连串所谓的“亚美尼亚”皇帝。他们的一份较长名单（由阿东茨提出）已被后来学者筛选缩减为几个“不言自明”的例子，包括菲利皮科斯·巴尔达尼斯（711–713）、利奥五世（813–820）、瓦西里一世（867–886）、罗曼努斯一世·拉卡佩努斯（920–944）和约安尼斯一世·齐米斯凯斯（969–976）。
然而正如我们所见，罗曼努斯一世·拉卡佩努斯的例子几乎谈不上不言自明，而且当我们追溯其余

人的脚注线索时——更不用说莫里斯（582–602）、希拉克略（610–641）或尼基弗鲁斯一世（802–811）了——显而易见，这些自信的断言建立在沙土之上，只是通过不加批判的重复才得以确立。但在我们细看学者用哪些可疑的方法造出这些亚美尼亚皇帝之前，我们还得再次追问：究竟在断言什么。当他本人、他的臣民或任何真正的亚美尼亚人都不承认他是亚美尼亚人时，称一位皇帝为“亚美尼亚人”意味着什么？史料对这样的出身只字未提，又该如何解释？当他的语言、宗教、政治归属和文化面貌全都是罗马的时候？

en: The answer to these questions is that we are saying nothing that has any literal content, but it only seems meaningful because it draws its substance from the vigorous claims of Armenian national historiography. This, like modern Greek national historiography, has benefited from the dismissive way in which scholarship treats Roman ethnicity. To clarify, we are not interested here in
ancestry but in

ethnicity. It was in fact possible, albeit rare, for Roman emperors to have “ethnic” profiles. But these are noted in the sources, as contemporaries were quite capable of making observations about ethnicity. Septimius Severus had Punic North African traits.
Zeno was an Isaurian, which was explicitly held against him as making him less than fully Roman.
