Michael II was said to be affiliated in some way with the heretical sect of the Athinganoi in central Asia Minor and to have followed some of their odd ways; he also seems to have had a speech impediment.
Alexios I Komnenos had a lisp.
Emperors are the most documented individuals, yet about none is it said that he spoke Greek with an Armenian accent, spoke Armenian at all, or followed Armenian customs in his private life.
zh: 这些问题的答案是：这样的称呼其实言之无物。它之所以显得有意义，是因为得到了亚美尼亚民族史学大力申说的支撑。这一点，如同现代希腊民族史学一样，得益于学界对待罗马族群性的那种轻蔑方式。澄清一下，这里所关心的是皇帝
，和
是两回事。罗马皇帝拥有“族群”面貌事实上是可能的，尽管罕见。但这些在史料中有所记载，因为同时代人完全有能力对族群性作出观察。塞普蒂米乌斯·塞维鲁有布匿北非特征。
芝诺是个伊苏里亚人，这一点被明确用来反对他，认为这使他不够完全罗马。
米海尔二世据说以某种方式与小亚细亚中部的阿辛加诺伊异端派别有关联，并遵循了他们的一些古怪做法；他似乎还有言语障碍。
阿莱克修斯一世·科穆宁说话时齿音不清。
关于皇帝的记录最为详尽，但其中没有一人的希腊语被记为带有亚美尼亚口音，也没有一人被记为会说亚美尼亚语，或在私下遵循亚美尼亚习俗。

en: The present section will first discuss some emperors to whom I believe Armenian ancestry has erroneously been attributed by modern scholarship. It will then discuss some emperors to whom an Armenian ancestry is attributed in some primary sources and assess the ways in which that factoid is relevant in our understanding of their reigns.
zh: 本节先讨论几位皇帝，我认为现代研究误把亚美尼亚出身归到他们身上。然后再谈几位原始史料确实提到有亚美尼亚祖先的皇帝，考察这项记载对理解他们的统治有多大帮助。

en: The alleged Armenian ancestry of the emperor Maurikios (582– 602) is largely unknown to historians who study his reign, even though it was “proven” by Adontz in 1934 and confirmed by Charanis in 1965.

No contemporary source—and there are many— mentions it. They all say that he came from Arabissos in Cappadocia, in the province of Armenia II. A historian writing during his reign, Euagrios, says that his family and name came from Old Rome, which may just be flattery, whereas an eighth-century western historian, Paul the Deacon, says that he was “a Cappadocian by race . . . the first emperor from the race of the Greeks,” whatever that means.
None of the names in his extended family are Armenian. It is only a later list of emperors, possibly from the eleventh century, which says that Maurikios was “by
an Armenian,” but this chronicle regularly converts provincial origins into
according to the ancient convention in the Roman empire that turned provincial origins into artificial ethnicities. Thus the emperor Markianos was “by
an Illyrian,” Leo I was “by
a Thracian,” Zeno was “by
an Isaurian,” Justin I was “a Thracian,” Tiberios II was “by
a Cappadocian,” and so on.

Maurikios was, as we said, from the province of Armenia II, a fact that would have been known to many Romans not only from geography but also because the bishopric of Arabissos belonged to the ecclesiastical province of Armenia, even in later times.
zh: 莫里斯皇帝（582–602）据说出自亚美尼亚，这一说法对研究其统治的史家来说大多是陌生的，尽管它已被阿东茨于1934年“证明”、并由查拉尼斯于1965年确认。
没有任何同时代史料——而且有很多——提到它。它们都说他来自卡帕多基亚的阿拉比索斯，在第二亚美尼亚行省。一位在他统治期间写作的史家欧阿格里奥斯说，他的家族和名字来自旧罗马，这可能只是奉承，而一位八世纪的西方史家执事保罗则说他是“种族上的卡帕多基亚人……第一位出自希腊人种族的皇帝”，无论那意味着什么。
他大家庭中的名字没有一个是亚美尼亚的。只有一份较晚的皇帝名单——可能来自十一世纪——说莫里斯“按族类（genos）是亚美尼亚人”，但这部编年史常用
（genos）表述各人的行省籍贯，沿用古罗马帝国以来把行省出身说成族群身份的习惯。因此马尔基安皇帝“按族类（genos）是伊利里亚人”，利奥一世“按族类（genos）是色雷斯人”，芝诺“按族类（genos）是伊苏里亚人”，查士丁一世是“色雷斯人”，提比略二世“按族类（genos）是卡帕多基亚人”，等等。
如我们所说，莫里斯来自第二亚美尼亚行省，许多罗马人无论按地理还是按教区划分，都知道有这个行省。阿拉比索斯主教区直到后来仍属亚美尼亚教省。

en: The “proof” of Maurikios’ Armenian origins is provided by a much later set of Armenian folktales told about the emperor. Adontz himself admitted that these tales were unhistorical in almost every way, but he selectively defended the nugget of the emperor’s origins in Armenia. Again, every punch is pulled for the purpose of making a Roman into an Armenian. Charanis conceded that the historical emperor Maurikios distrusted the Armenians, and seventh-century sources claim that he formulated aggressive policies against them.

Yet he tried to argue around these reports by reasoning that Maurikios’ intimate knowledge of the Armenians’ bad qualities—the grounds of his hostility—meant that he was one of them. (The same argument has been used by another historian, again with a straight face, for the emperor Nikephoros II Phokas: he was so hostile to the Armenians in his legal and military works that he must have been one himself.)

Charanis also has to argue around the fact that Maurikios’ Armenian ethnicity is not mentioned by a much earlier, and more sober, Armenian historian, pseudo-Sebeos (of the seventh century). Charanis responds by saying that this does not count because pseudo-Sebeos also does not mention the Armenian ancestry of the emperor Herakleios, which is a sacred cow of the Armenian fallacy. So let us take a closer look at Herakleios.
zh: 莫里斯亚美尼亚起源的“证据”，由一组晚得多的、关于这位皇帝的亚美尼亚民间故事提供。阿东茨本人承认这些故事几乎在各方面都不合历史，他却唯独坚持其中说皇帝出自亚美尼亚的一点可信。同样，为了把这位罗马人说成亚美尼亚人，批判史料的标准再次被放宽。查拉尼斯承认，历史上的莫里斯皇帝不信任亚美尼亚人，而七世纪的史料声称他制定了针对他们的侵略性政策。
然而他试图绕开这些报道来论证，推理说莫里斯正是因为熟知那些被认为是亚美尼亚人的缺点，才对他们抱有敌意，因此他自己必定也是亚美尼亚人。（另一位史家同样一本正经地把同一论点用于尼基弗鲁斯二世·福卡斯皇帝：他在其法律和军事著作中对亚美尼亚人如此敌视，以至于他必定自己就是亚美尼亚人。）
查拉尼斯还不得不绕开这样一个事实：莫里斯的亚美尼亚族群性没有被一位早得多、也更清醒的亚美尼亚史家伪塞贝奥斯（七世纪）提到。查拉尼斯回应说这不算数，因为伪塞贝奥斯也没有提到希拉克略皇帝的亚美尼亚血统，而那是亚美尼亚谬误不可触碰的信条。那么让我们更仔细地看看希拉克略。

en: The Armenian ethnic origin of the emperor Herakleios (610–641) takes the prize for fiction masquerading as history. Even the

children: Prosopography of the Later Roman Empire,

en: the standard reference work of the field, asserts that “the family was Armenian,” a conclusion that is more tentatively endorsed in the most recent biography of the emperor.

The scholarly imagination has here run riot: not only was he Armenian, Herakleios was “related to the Arsacids of Armenia and came from the Arsacid princedom of Carenitis” (i.e., Karin). His Greek name was a translation of Vahagn, an Armenian pagan god sometimes equated with Herakles.
He may have been the great-great-grandson of Hovanes Arshakuni.
“Presumably he was bilingual”—though it is immediately conceded that there is no proof for that.
His politics and military strategy are examined in light of his Armenian ethnicity and his relationship to “his Armenian compatriots.”
zh: 希拉克略皇帝（610–641）的亚美尼亚族群起源，在以虚构冒充历史的说法中最为离谱。即便是学界的标准参考书《晚期罗马帝国人物志》（Prosopography of the Later Roman Empire）也断言“这个家族是亚美尼亚的”，而这一结论在该皇帝最新的传记中得到了较为审慎的认可。
学者在这里任由想象驰骋。按照这些说法，希拉克略不仅是亚美尼亚人，还“与亚美尼亚的阿尔萨克王朝有亲缘关系，出自阿尔萨克王朝的卡雷尼蒂斯公国”（即卡林）。他的希腊名字是瓦哈格恩的翻译，后者是一位亚美尼亚异教神，有时被等同于赫拉克勒斯。
他可能是霍瓦内斯·阿尔沙库尼的玄孙。
“想必他是双语者”——尽管随即就承认对此没有证据。
还有人依据他所谓的亚美尼亚出身，以及他与“亚美尼亚同胞”的关系，来解释他的施政与军事战略。

en: Just so that we are clear,

children: there is not a single primary source

en: that says that Herakleios was an Armenian. The statements in the paragraph above have been woven out of thin air. The biographer I mentioned, Walter Kaegi, admits that “we have no evidence on what Armenian consciousness, if any, Heraclius possessed.”

But identity without awareness is just racial thinking. The later Byzantine sources call Herakleios a Libyan, because that was where he was based when he rebelled against Phokas in 602, and a Cappadocian.

Moreover, none of the names in his extended family are Armenian, and this in an age when Armenian generals in Roman service kept their native names and did not always switch to Graeco-Roman ones. So where does the error come from?
zh: 为了说清楚，

children: 没有任何一部原始史料

zh: 说希拉克略是亚美尼亚人。上面那段话中的陈述都是凭空编造出来的。我提到的那位传记作者沃尔特·卡埃吉承认，“关于希拉克略拥有何种亚美尼亚意识（如果有的话），我们没有证据”。
但没有自觉的认同不过是种族思维。较晚的拜占庭史料称希拉克略为利比亚人，因为他以那里为基地起兵反对福卡斯，也称他为卡帕多基亚人。
此外，他的家族成员没有一个用亚美尼亚名字，而这还是在这样一个时代：在罗马服役的亚美尼亚将军保留本土名字，并不总是改用希腊—罗马名字。那么这个错误从何而来？

en: The fiction of Herakleios’ Armenian ancestry is based on a single sentence in the historian Theophylaktos Simokattes that refers to the military career of the emperor’s father, also named Herakleios. In late 587, Herakleios the Elder was a general serving under Philippikos, the

The latter had just found out (in Constantinople) that he had been replaced by Priskos. He wrote to Herakleios the Elder in the east ordering him “to leave the army and return to his own city in Armenia,” transferring the army over to Narses, the commander at Konstantine (a city in the province of Osrhoene).
zh: 希拉克略亚美尼亚血统的虚构，基于史家塞奥菲拉克托斯·西莫卡特斯著作中的单独一句话，那句话涉及皇帝父亲（同样名叫希拉克略）的军旅生涯。587年末，老希拉克略是在东方方面军统帅（magister militum per Orientem）菲利皮科斯麾下服役的一位将军。后者刚刚（在君士坦丁堡）得知自己已被普里斯科斯取代。他致信在东方的老希拉克略，命令他“离开军队，回到他自己在亚美尼亚的城”，并把军队移交给纳尔塞斯——君士坦丁娜城（奥斯若恩行省的一座城市）的指挥官。

en: This passage cannot bear the weight that has been placed on it. First, it does not call Herakleios the Elder an Armenian. It says only that “his own city” was in Armenia, which certainly means Roman Armenia, the four (militarized) provinces of that name that were populated by both Romans and Armenians. Second, “his own city” in Armenia certainly refers to Herakleios’ command headquarters, not his home town. It would make no sense in the context of the narrative for Philippikos to send Herakleios “home.” Herakleios was not being decommissioned but being given orders for moving the army within his command territory. This was exactly how the translators of Theophylaktos understood the passage, one of whom, Michael Whitby, is the leading historian of the wars in question: Herakleios was being sent back to his headquarters at Theodosioupolis (Erzurum).
He was still active in the same military post for the next couple of years: he had not been sent “home.”
There is no ethnicity here, no proof that “he was born in the region of Karin.”

The passage says and implies nothing about where Herakleios the Elder was “from.” Even if he was “from” a Roman city in Armenia, such as Theodosioupolis, that would not mean he was “an Armenian.” Those places had been crawling with Roman soldiers, officers, and their families ever since Justinian established the massive field army
manned largely (and deliberately) with non-Armenians. Justinian had also established a civilian, legal, and bureaucratic apparatus tasked with imposing Roman law on the four Armenian provinces.

As with the theme of Armeniakon, we should not mistake administrative labels with demography and ethnicity. The four Armenian themes had been formed in part by imperial expansion into Armenian lands but also through the subdivision of the former Roman province of Cappadocia. Even if Herakleios’ “home” or residence was in one of them—which the passage in Theophylaktos does not suggest—that would say nothing about his ethnicity, and even less about the ethnicity of his son.
zh: 这段文字不足以支持那样的结论。首先，它没有称老希拉克略为亚美尼亚人。它只说“他自己的城市”在亚美尼亚，这无疑指罗马亚美尼亚，即那个名字的四个实行军事部署的行省，那里住着罗马人和亚美尼亚人。其次，在亚美尼亚的“他自己的城市”无疑指希拉克略的指挥总部，而非他的家乡。在叙事语境中，菲利皮科斯把希拉克略送“回家”是说不通的。希拉克略不是被解职，而是被下达了在其指挥辖区内调动军队的命令。这正是塞奥菲拉克托斯的译者们理解这段文字的方式，其中一位迈克尔·惠特比是相关战争的首要史家：希拉克略是被送回他在狄奥多西乌波利斯（埃尔祖鲁姆）的总部。
此后几年他仍在同一军职上活跃：可见他并未被调回家乡。
这里没有族群性，没有证据表明“他出生在卡林地区”。
这段文字对老希拉克略“来自”哪里既未明说也未暗示。即便他“来自”亚美尼亚的一座罗马城市，例如狄奥多西乌波利斯，那也不意味着他是“一个亚美尼亚人”。自从查士丁尼建立那支有意以非亚美尼亚人为主体组成的庞大亚美尼亚方面军（per Armeniam）以来，那些地方就挤满了罗马士兵、军官及其家属。查士丁尼还建立了一套民政、法律和官僚机构，负责在那四个亚美尼亚行省推行罗马法。
正如亚美尼亚军区的情况，我们不应把行政标签与人口结构和族群性混为一谈。这四个亚美尼亚行省的形成，部分是由于帝国向亚美尼亚土地的扩张，但也通过对原罗马卡帕多基亚行省的细分。即便希拉克略的“家”或居所在其中之一——塞奥菲拉克托斯的那段文字并未暗示这一点——那也说明不了他的族群性，更说明不了他儿子的族群性。

en: Another house of cards collapses here: there is no proof that Herakleios was an Armenian. The seventh-century Armenian historian pseudo-Sebeos, who wrote but a generation later, mentions Herakleios the Elder and his son many times but never says that they were Armenians.
As far as I know, no Armenian historian calls Herakleios an Armenian. Never has the Armenian fallacy built up so much on the basis of so little, as it has here.
zh: 又一座纸牌屋在这里倒塌：没有证据表明希拉克略是亚美尼亚人。七世纪的亚美尼亚史家伪塞贝奥斯只晚了一代，书中多次提到老希拉克略和他的儿子，却从未说他们是亚美尼亚人。
据我所知，没有亚美尼亚史家称希拉克略为亚美尼亚人。亚美尼亚谬误从未像在这里这样，凭如此稀少的材料搭建出如此多的说法。

en: Ioannes I Tzimiskes (969–976) is also widely considered to have been “an Armenian,” but the grounds for this are extremely weak. First, he came from the Armeniakon theme, but the name of this theme, as we saw above, did not reflect its demography. The second reason is his nickname—Tzimiskes is not a family name—which is said in a history written by a Roman contemporary to be an Armenian word referring to the emperor’s short stature, in which case he must have earned it as an adult.

For all we know, it was given to him by Armenian soldiers serving under him. A much later and far less reliable historian, Matthew of Edessa, claimed that the nickname came from the similar-sounding name of the village in which Tzimiskes was allegedly born, near Hozat in modern Turkey (also in the Armeniakon theme, broadly defined). However, this claim occurs in the midst of a purely fictional romance that requires Tzimiskes to have been born in that area for dramatic narrative purposes. It may simply be an invention based on the similarity of the names and, besides, it does not make Tzimiskes into an Armenian to begin with, and neither does Matthew nor any other source claim that he was one.
Nor, as far as we know, was Tzimiskes related to any Armenians. No ethnicity or even distant ancestry can be proposed based on such evidence.
zh: 约安尼斯一世·齐米斯凯斯（969–976）也被广泛认为是“一个亚美尼亚人”，但这一点的依据极其薄弱。首先，他来自亚美尼亚军区，但正如我们上面所见，这个军区的名字并不反映其人口结构。第二个理由是他的绰号——齐米斯凯斯不是家族姓——一位罗马同时代人撰写的史书说它是一个亚美尼亚词，指这位皇帝身材矮小，若如此，他必定是在成年后才得到它的。

这个绰号也可能是他麾下的亚美尼亚士兵给他起的。一位晚得多、也远不可靠的史家埃德萨的马太声称，这个绰号来自据称齐米斯凯斯出生的那个村庄读音相近的地名，该村靠近现代土耳其的霍扎特（广义上也在亚美尼亚军区）。然而，这一声称出现在一段纯属虚构的传奇之中，为了讲出这个富有戏剧性的故事，齐米斯凯斯就得出生在那里。它可能只是基于名字相似的一种编造，而且它本来就没有使齐米斯凯斯成为亚美尼亚人，马太或任何其他史料也都没有声称他是亚美尼亚人。
据我们所知，齐米斯凯斯也与任何亚美尼亚人没有亲缘关系。基于这样的证据，无法断定他属于某一族群，甚至连他有这样的远祖也无法确定。

en: Unlike Maurikios, Herakleios, and Tzimiskes, there are other emperors who are said by roughly contemporary sources to have had Armenian ancestry. Still, in not one case can we say that these were “Armenian emperors” in any meaningful sense. As far as we know, they were all Romans of (possible) Armenian ancestry. None of them exhibits any cultural or biographical traits that would associate him with Armenia. Moreover, individually they present certain idiosyncrasies in their alleged Armenianness that are worth examining.
zh: 与莫里斯、希拉克略和齐米斯凯斯不同，还有其他一些皇帝被大致同时代的史料说成有亚美尼亚血统。即使如此，要称他们中的任何一人为“亚美尼亚皇帝”，也没有什么实质意义。据我们所知，他们都是（可能）有亚美尼亚血统的罗马人。他们中没有一人表现出任何会把他与亚美尼亚联系起来的文化或传记特征。此外，他们各自的亚美尼亚出身说，都有值得仔细考察之处。

en: Philippikos Bardanes (711–713) is said to have been “an Armenian by
” or “a Persarmenian by

” For all we know, he was of Persian rather than Armenian ancestry, but we lack an Iranian lobby to push for its own “ethnic rights” in Byzantine Studies. Our sources for his origin also condemn him for his evil ecclesiastical policies and erroneous theology (Monothelitism).

They may be highlighting his ethnicity to make him look more foreign, though there is no reason to think that they were simply inventing it. The move to link his ethnicity and doctrinal views has been made even more explicitly by modern historians.

But how far back did Bardanes’ ethnic background lie? His father Nikephoros was active at the Roman court in the 660s, under Konstas II, which means that Bardanes was probably born and raised in Romanía; possibly, his father was too.
The suggestion that they were descended from the fifth-century Armenian hero Vardan II Mamikonian is a modern fiction.
A number of sources testify to Bardanes’ tutoring, scholarly interests, learning, and eloquence, which were all in Greek.

It is likely, in that age of iron, that he highlighted these attributes of elite culture in order to compensate for his ethnic past, which is why many sources comment on them. We have seen how provincials with possible ethnic origins (e.g., Niketas
) used classical learning to showcase their Roman credentials.
zh: 菲利皮科斯·巴尔达尼斯（711–713）据说“按族类（genos）是亚美尼亚人”或“按族类（genos）是波斯亚美尼亚人”。凭现有材料，他其实也可能出自波斯，但我们缺少一个伊朗游说集团在拜占庭研究中为它自己的“族群权利”奔走。关于他起源的史料也谴责他邪恶的教会政策和错误的神学（一志论）。
它们可能是在突出他的族群性以使他显得更异邦，尽管没有理由认为它们只是在凭空编造。把他的族群性与教义观点联系起来的举动，已被现代史家做得更加明确。
但巴尔达尼斯的族群背景要追溯到多远？他的父亲尼基弗鲁斯在660年代、君士坦斯二世治下活跃于罗马宫廷，这意味着巴尔达尼斯很可能在罗曼尼亚出生和长大；可能他父亲也是。
说他们是五世纪亚美尼亚英雄瓦尔丹二世·马米科尼扬的后裔，这是一种现代虚构。
若干史料证明了巴尔达尼斯的受教、学术兴趣、学识和雄辩，而这些全都是希腊语的。
在那个严酷的时代，他很可能突出自己掌握的精英文化，以免祖先的外族出身让人看轻他，这就是为什么许多史料评论它们。我们已经看到，可能有外族祖源的行省居民（例如尼基塔斯行政长官（magistros））如何用古典学识来展示他们的罗马资历。

en: Philippikos Bardanes is especially interesting in this connection because of his decision to expel all Armenians from the empire, forcing them to seek refuge among the Arabs, though the extent to which this was enforced is unknown. This measure followed upon a decree ordering all Armenians to accept the authority of the patriarch of Constantinople, though it is unclear whether this decree was issued by Philippikos or Justinian II, his predecessor.

The perverse illogic of the Armenian fallacy would link this anti-Armenian policy to Philippikos’ Armenian ethnicity. In reality, it shows that despite his ancestry he was not, and did not consider himself to be, “an Armenian,” as some modern historians call him.

Interestingly, a later (tenth-century?) Armenian history does call him “an Armenian noble.” Was its author engaging in an early version of the Armenian fallacy, making guesses based on the emperor’s name alone? This would explain why the attribution is so vague, lacking the details of family affiliation that Armenian memory so cherished.
zh: 菲利皮科斯·巴尔达尼斯在这方面尤其有意思，因为他决定把所有亚美尼亚人驱逐出帝国，迫使他们到阿拉伯人中间寻求庇护，尽管这一措施被执行到什么程度不得而知。这一措施继一道命令所有亚美尼亚人接受君士坦丁堡牧首权威的敕令之后，尽管不清楚这道敕令是菲利皮科斯还是他的前任查士丁尼二世颁布的。
按照亚美尼亚谬误那套反常的逻辑，会把这一反亚美尼亚政策与菲利皮科斯的亚美尼亚族群性联系起来。实际上，它表明尽管他有那样的血统，他却不是、也不认为自己是“一个亚美尼亚人”，而某些现代史家却这样称他。
有意思的是，一部较晚的（十世纪？）亚美尼亚史书确实称他为“一个亚美尼亚贵族”。它的作者是也在按某种早期形式的亚美尼亚谬误推论，仅凭皇帝的名字作猜测吗？这就能解释为什么这一认定如此含糊，缺少亚美尼亚记忆如此珍视的家族归属细节。

en: Three more emperors are said in the earliest sources about them to have had an Armenian ancestry: Artabasdos (a rebel general who briefly took power in Constantinople in the early 740s), Leon V (813– 820), and Basileios I (867–886). We do not know enough about the first to have an interesting discussion of his ethnicity.
Leon V’s ancestry is said to have been Armenian, Assyrian, and Amalekite (a biblical ethnonym), whatever exactly those terms may have meant in a late eighth-century context.
Like Philippikos Bardanes, he was raised in the empire; his father Bardas was a
at the court.

The tales of his ethnic ancestries are told by later Iconophile texts in order to blacken him further as an Iconoclast heretic, though this does not mean that we can write them off as mere polemic. However, we have no evidence for how Leon V acknowledged, tried to hide or counter, or ameliorated his “ethnic” background as emperor. Matters are different when we turn to Basileios I, however. His dynasty, the Macedonians, produced a phantasmagoric account of Basileios’ descent from a royal house of Armenia as well as from Alexander the Great and Constantine the Great. We are here squarely in the realm of the rhetoric of ethnicity, which means that we must approach the subject from a different angle.
zh: 还有三位皇帝在关于他们的最早史料中被说成有亚美尼亚血统：阿尔塔巴斯多斯（一位叛乱将军，740年代初曾在君士坦丁堡短暂掌权）、利奥五世（813–820）和瓦西里一世（867–886）。我们对第一位了解不够，还不足以讨论他的族群身份。
利奥五世的血统据说可追溯到亚美尼亚人、亚述人和亚玛力人（一个圣经族名），无论这些词在八世纪晚期的语境中究竟意味着什么。
像菲利皮科斯·巴尔达尼斯一样，他在帝国长大；他的父亲巴尔达斯是宫廷中的一位帕特里基奥斯（patrikios）。

关于他族群血统的故事由较晚的圣像拥护者文本讲述，目的是进一步进一步贬斥这个属于毁像派的异端，尽管这不意味着我们可以把它们当作纯粹的论战而一笔勾销。然而，我们没有证据表明利奥五世作为皇帝怎样看待自己的“族群”背景，是承认、尝试掩盖、加以反驳，还是淡化处理。不过当我们转向瓦西里一世时，情况就不同了。他的王朝——马其顿王朝——制造了一套光怪陆离的说法，称瓦西里出自亚美尼亚的一个王室，也出自亚历山大大帝和君士坦丁大帝。我们在这里完全处于族群性修辞的领域，这意味着我们必须从另一个角度来处理这个主题。

en: The Politics of Armenian Ethnicity
zh: 亚美尼亚族群身份与政治

en: In Romanía, calling someone an Armenian or claiming an Armenian origin for oneself could be a banal piece of information, but sometimes such claims played into a contested field of ethnic stereotypes, religious animosities, genealogical pretensions, and the politics of belonging and exclusion. To make sense of this chaotic scene, we may start by drawing a general distinction between Roman views of Armenians, including ethnic Armenians who were imperial subjects, and Roman views of Romans who had Armenian ancestry but were in all relevant ways assimilated to Roman norms. The latter category includes almost all the “Armenians” discussed in this chapter. Looking at their careers and diversity, from emperors to saints, it appears that Roman society did not treat them any differently than other Romans. Assimilation was possible and did not carry an ethnic stigma. The Armenian ancestry of these individuals may have been something that they wished to have remembered and associated with their names, though we cannot know. There are a few cases, however, where it was invoked polemically to tarnish their reputations, for example against Philippikos Bardanes and Leon V who were (in retrospect) regarded as heretical and therefore alien to the Christian Roman order.
zh: 在罗曼尼亚，称某人为亚美尼亚人或为自己声称亚美尼亚起源，有时只是说起一件平常的事，有时却会牵涉族群成见、宗教敌意、攀附门第，以及谁有资格加入罗马共同体的争论。要理解这一混乱的场景，我们可以先作一个总体区分：一是罗马人对亚美尼亚人的看法，包括作为帝国臣民的族群亚美尼亚人；二是罗马人对那些有亚美尼亚血统、但在所有相关方面都已同化于罗马规范的罗马人的看法。后一范畴几乎包括本章讨论的所有“亚美尼亚人”。看看他们的生涯和多样性，从皇帝到圣徒都有，罗马社会似乎并未区别对待他们。同化是可能的，而且不带族群污名。这些个人的亚美尼亚血统可能是他们希望被人记住、并与他们的名字联系起来的东西，尽管我们无从知道。然而也有少数例子，有人在论战中搬出他们的祖源，以败坏其声望，例如针对菲利皮科斯·巴尔达尼斯和利奥五世，他们（在回顾中）被视为异端，因而与基督教罗马秩序格格不入。

en: This stigma was effective because unassimilated ethnic Armenians were generally associated with negative stereotypes. Of course, any people regarded by the Romans as foreign in terms of ethnicity and culture were bound to be viewed negatively. This was certainly the case with the Armenians, starting already in late antiquity. “We live here among Armenian barbarians,” wrote the Roman bishops of Armenia II in 458, “who are of the faith, to be sure, but they lack Roman eloquence.”

But when the Armenian Church refused to accept the Council of Chalcedon, its followers in later centuries were deemed heretical as well as barbarous in Roman eyes, resulting in theological polemics against “the Armenians.” These prejudices could combine into vicious images, as we find in a poem attributed to the famous female hymnographer of the ninth century, Kasia (or Kasiane):
zh: 这种污名之所以有效，是因为罗马人通常对尚未同化的亚美尼亚族人抱有负面成见。当然，任何在族群和文化上被罗马人视为异邦的民族，都必定被负面看待。亚美尼亚人无疑如此，早在晚期古代就已开始。“我们这里住在亚美尼亚蛮族中间，”第二亚美尼亚行省的罗马主教们在458年写道，“他们固然有信仰，却缺少罗马的雄辩。”
但当亚美尼亚教会拒绝接受卡尔西顿会议的决议后，在后来的世纪里，其信徒在罗马人眼中既被视为异端又被视为蛮族，由此产生了针对“亚美尼亚人”的神学论战。这些偏见相互叠加，可能造出极为恶毒的形象，正如我们在归于九世纪著名女圣诗作者卡西亚（或卡西亚涅）名下的一首诗中所见：

en: The terrible race of the Armenians is deceitful and extremely vile, fanatical, deranged, and malignant, puffed up with hot air and full of slyness. A wise man said correctly about them that Armenians are vile when they live in obscurity, even more vile when they become famous, and most vile in all ways when they become rich. When they become filthy rich and honored, then to all they seem as vileness heaped upon vileness.
zh: 亚美尼亚人这个可怕的种族狡诈而极其卑劣，狂热、错乱而恶毒，满口大话，又诡计多端。一位智者正确地论及他们说：亚美尼亚人卑微时卑劣，出名时更卑劣，富有时则在各方面都最卑劣。他们若富得流油，又受人尊崇，人人都会觉得他们卑劣到了极点。

en: The

children: Life of Saint Euthymios the Younger

en: (ca. 900) refers to a monk Ioseph on Mt. Athos as being a simple and good man at heart, “despite his Armenian origin.”

We see that ethnocultural identifications were present even in this far-off uninhabited corner of the monastic world, in a text written by and for Romans. Armenians were regarded as outsiders even when they were inside the empire. When the empire expanded dramatically in the tenth and eleventh centuries, these slurs could be directed against many of the inhabitants of the new eastern provinces. We have the will of one Eustathios Boïlas who, under adverse circumstances that he does not elucidate, found himself living there in the mid-eleventh century: “I became an emigrant from the land which bore me . . . and I settled among alien nations with strange religion and tongue.” He later explains that these were Armenians, whom he mentions right after “snakes, scorpions, and wild beasts.”
zh: 《小圣欧蒂米奥斯传》（Life of Saint Euthymios the Younger，约900年）提到阿索斯山上的一位修士约瑟夫，说他内心是个纯朴善良的人，“尽管他出身于亚美尼亚人”。

我们看到，即便在这个偏僻、人烟稀少的修道场所，罗马人写给罗马人看的书，仍会留意一人的族群文化出身。亚美尼亚人即便身处帝国之内也被视为外人。当帝国在十、十一世纪急剧扩张时，这些贬称可能被指向新东部行省的许多居民。我们有一份欧斯塔提奥斯·博伊拉斯的遗嘱，他在十一世纪中叶、因某些他未细说的困境，到了那里生活：“我成了离开生养我之地的移民……我定居在宗教和语言都陌生的异族中间。”他后来解释说这些是亚美尼亚人，他把他们紧接在“蛇、蝎子和野兽”之后提到。

en: It is often asserted that the Byzantines respected the fighting prowess of the Armenians, who were allegedly sturdy and valiant soldiers. This probably was the case, given the Armenians’ prominent role in the Roman army for so many centuries, but it finds scant expression in Byzantine literature, including in the military manuals and histories. Instead, they are often depicted as unreliable, undisciplined, shifty, and prone to banditry: “The Armenians carry out sentry duty poorly and carelessly . . . after all, they are only Armenians.”
(Conversely, Armenian literature contained plenty of recriminations and stereotypes against Romans.)
zh: 人们常断言拜占庭人尊重亚美尼亚人的战斗本领，据说他们是强悍英勇的士兵。鉴于亚美尼亚人许多世纪以来在罗马军队中的突出角色，这很可能属实，但拜占庭文献，包括军事手册和史书，几乎没有表达过这种看法。相反，他们常被描绘为不可靠、不守纪律、狡猾且易于沦为匪盗：“亚美尼亚人站岗既不可靠，也不仔细……毕竟，他们不过是亚美尼亚人。”
（反过来，亚美尼亚文学也包含大量针对罗马人的指责和成见。）

en: These negative images were not limited to elite literature or classicizing tropes that recycled stale ancient polemics. To the contrary, they were produced and most intensely disseminated in the middle Byzantine period, when so many Armenians had entered the empire. We can even speak of popular prejudice in this connection. In the twelfth century, we hear of mimes who performed comic sketches about Arabs and Armenians.

With such prejudice at hand, it is not surprising that attacks against emperors and other individuals could also target their (real or only alleged) Armenian origins as aggravating factors. When the patriarch Theodosios Boradiotes made a seemingly underhanded comment to the emperor Andronikos I Komnenos (1183–1185), the latter said, “‘Behold our profound Armenian,’ because it was said that his family had Armenian roots.”
Romans of Armenian descent might have faced this commonly, even though they were accepted at all levels of Roman life. This was likely possible because they were not Armenians in any meaningful way.
zh: 这些负面形象并不限于精英文学，也不限于重复陈腐古代论战的古典化套路。恰恰相反，它们是在中期拜占庭时期被制造并最强烈地传播的，当时有那么多亚美尼亚人进入了帝国。在这方面我们甚至可以谈论民众偏见。十二世纪，我们听说有表演关于阿拉伯人和亚美尼亚人滑稽小品的滑稽戏演员。
正因为有这样的成见，有人攻击皇帝和其他人物时，往往连他们真实或传闻中的亚美尼亚出身也拿来说事。当牧首狄奥多西奥斯·博拉迪奥特斯对安德罗尼库斯一世·科穆宁皇帝（1183–1185）作出一句看似阴险的评论时，后者说，“‘看哪，我们这位高深的亚美尼亚人’，因为据说他的家族有亚美尼亚根源”。
亚美尼亚裔罗马人可能经常面对这种情况，尽管他们在罗马生活的各个层面都被接受。这之所以可能，很可能是因为他们在有实质意义的层面上早已不再是亚美尼亚人。

en: Still, it is possible that the “melting pot” model does not fully account for the Armenian experience in Romanía. Was it possible for assimilated Armenian-Romans to be proud of their Armenian ancestry? Could it be used to advantage, or even invented for that purpose when it did not exist? This is more difficult to document, but the possibility is enticing. To turn to the field of U.S. sociology, the familiar melting pot model may work as a kind of baseline, but it has been found to be deficient. In particular, it has failed to explain the fact that some groups do not assimilate as quickly or as well as others, or are blocked from assimilating because of racial traits that they cannot leave behind. Some groups may react to persecution or discrimination by withdrawing from the mainstream and forming a separate community (we will see in Chapter 6 that the Paulicians may count as such a group). But other groups, especially from economically better-off immigrant communities, for whom assimilation and “whiteness” is possible, may nevertheless choose to selectively cultivate ethnic networks and affiliations and activate them in advantageous contexts. Moreover, others have failed or refused to entirely forget about their Old World past and continue to cultivate links to it through narratives, ethnic food, dress, and religious customs. This is sometimes called “symbolic ethnicity” and seen as sociologically trivial, for its scope is limited to practices that do not offend the dominant culture.

Yet these “white ethnics” (especially Greek, Italian, and Irish Americans) create community organizations and maintain affective ties and networks, for all that they are assimilated to the mainstream.
zh: 不过，“熔炉”模型有可能无法完全解释亚美尼亚人在罗曼尼亚的经历。已被同化的亚美尼亚裔罗马人有可能以自己的亚美尼亚血统为荣吗？这种血统能否被用来谋取好处，甚至在并不存在时为此目的而被虚构出来？这一点更难找到文献证据，但这种可能性引人入胜。转向美国社会学领域，人们熟悉的熔炉模型或许可以用来考察一般情形，但研究者已经发现其中有不足。尤其是，它未能解释这样一个事实：有些群体同化得不如其他群体那样快、那样好，或者因为无法摆脱的种族特征而被阻挡在同化之外。有些群体可能以退出主流、形成独立社群的方式来回应迫害或歧视（我们将在第6章看到，保罗派或许可以算作这样一个群体）。但另一些群体，尤其是来自经济上较富裕的移民社群、能够同化并获得“白人身份”的群体，也可能有选择地维系同族关系，在有利的场合加以利用。此外，还有一些群体未能或不愿完全忘却自己在旧大陆的过去，继续通过叙事、本族饮食、服饰与宗教习俗来维系与它的联系。这有时被称为“象征性族群性”，并在社会学上被视为无足轻重，因为其范围仅限于那些不冒犯主流文化的实践。
然而这些“白人族群”（尤其是希腊裔、意大利裔和爱尔兰裔美国人）尽管已融入主流社会，却仍创建社群组织、维系情感纽带与网络。

en: At present, a sociology of the Byzantine “ethnics” lies beyond our reach, especially when the basic parameters of Roman ethnicity in Romanía are misunderstood by the field on a fundamental level. In addition, we are not in a position to reconstruct the thick context and social valence of ethnic claims, or, in many cases, the biography of those who make them. All I can offer here are some preliminary remarks.
zh: 目前，我们还无法对拜占庭社会中的“族裔群体”作出社会学分析，尤其是当学界在根本层面上误解了罗曼尼亚的罗马族群身份有哪些基本特点时。此外，我们也无法复原各种族群身份说法的具体来由及其社会意义，而且在许多情况下，也无法重构提出这些宣称者的生平。我在此所能提供的，只是一些初步的评述。

en: We have seen that gestures of affective ethnicity were made by the first generation of Armenian Romans. Maria the Younger gave half of her children Armenian names. Alexios Mosele lived in a manor house in Constantinople that was presumably named after his city or land of origin in Armenia (whether or not he had ever been there, and more likely not). The language would certainly have been spoken among some assimilated Armenians, just as we saw a network of successfully integrated Persian-speakers in Constantinople in 867. Sometimes origins were remembered, rather than forgotten or actively suppressed. The

children: Life of Saint Maria the Younger

en: openly discloses that her father was Armenian but makes sure to reveal that he was powerful and honored by the emperor. The historian Genesios took pride in his grandfather Konstantinos “the Armenian” and sought to praise him at every turn in his narrative. It is also likely that historical sources label individuals as having a (proximate or distant) Armenian origin not only because that was a known fact about them but because they chose to broadcast it and link their name to it. In other words, being of Armenian origin may have had a positive value that pushed against the negative stereotypes that we saw above.
zh: 我们已经看到，第一代亚美尼亚裔罗马人已用不同方式表达过对祖先族群的感情。小圣玛丽亚给一半的孩子起了亚美尼亚名字。阿莱克修斯·莫塞莱住在君士坦丁堡的一座庄园宅邸里，那座宅邸想必是以他在亚美尼亚的祖居城市或地方命名的（无论他是否曾去过那里，而更可能的是从未去过）。这种语言无疑会在一些已被同化的亚美尼亚人中间使用，正如我们在867年的君士坦丁堡看到过一个成功融入的说波斯语者网络。有时，起源是被铭记的，而非被遗忘或刻意压制。《小圣玛丽亚传》公开透露她的父亲是亚美尼亚人，但特意表明他权势显赫、深受皇帝尊荣。史家格内西奥斯以自己的祖父“亚美尼亚人”君士坦丁为荣，并力图在叙事中处处颂扬他。文献记下某人远近不一的亚美尼亚祖源，有可能是由于出身人所共知，也有可能是当事人愿意宣扬此事，好让人一听到他的名字便想起这样的家世。换言之，拥有亚美尼亚起源可能具有一种正面价值，足以抵抗我们上文所见的那些负面刻板印象。

en: It is not difficult to see what that value was for social elites. Their ethnicity may have been a liability in some contexts in Roman society, but being perceived as nobility or as a member of a royal family (even if only a foreign one) conferred prestige in contexts that may have mattered more to them for political and social purposes. Already in the early seventh century, a governor of Ravenna, Isaakios, took pride in his ethnicity in the epitaph carved on his sarcophagus: “He was the great jewel of the whole of Armenia, an Armenian from a glorious family,” but it also says that “he kept Rome safe as a general.”
This was a Roman general who expressed himself publicly in Greek, even when in Italy, and was certainly Byzantine Orthodox too (he was buried in San Vitale).
zh: 不难看出这种价值对社会精英意味着什么。在罗马社会的一些场合，外族出身或许是个负担。不过，贵族或王室门第，哪怕是外国王室，也能带来声望，在政治和社交上更要紧的场合或许尤其有用。早在七世纪初，拉文纳的一位总督伊萨克就在刻于其石棺上的墓志铭中以自己的族群性为荣：“他是全亚美尼亚的璀璨瑰宝，一个出身显赫家族的亚美尼亚人”，但铭文也说“他以将军之职护佑罗马安宁”。
这是一位罗马将军，即便身处意大利也公开用希腊语表达自己，而且无疑也是拜占庭正教徒（他被安葬在圣维塔莱教堂）。

en: The threads of this discussion come together in the emperor Basileios I (867–886). I close this chapter with a closer look at how the politics of ethnicity played out in his case. Basileios was of humble, possibly peasant origin, from Macedonia, which is why he and the dynasty that he founded were called “the Macedonians.” He migrated to Constantinople to seek a better life and skillfully maneuvered and murdered his way to the throne. To the extent that the sources allow us to see it, his cultural profile is entirely Roman with no trace of foreign culture, and panegyrical texts written about him during his reign highlight his humble origins to cast him as a new David.

But an effort to mythologize this emperor was already under way. When Basileios I died, his son and heir Leon VI composed a funeral oration for him that claimed that he was descended from the royal line of the Arsacids, who were in turn descended from the Persian king Artaxerxes I (465–424 bc), who ruled over a large empire.

The Arsacids were, in fact, of Iranian origin, and it was only a later branch of them that ruled Armenia. But Leon’s boast lies under the shadow of an infamous scandal. The patriarch Photios is alleged by his enemies of having forged, during the period of his ten-year deposition (867–877), a genealogy for Basileios, trying to flatter his way back into the emperor’s favor by tracing his ancestry to the Arsacid Armenian king Tiridates the Great (d. 330), who converted to Christianity.
If the story is true, then Leon’s funeral oration was based on a forgery.
zh: 本章讨论的诸条线索汇聚于皇帝瓦西里一世（867–886）身上。我以更细致地审视族群性政治在他这一案例中如何运作来结束本章。瓦西里出身寒微，可能是农民，来自马其顿，正因如此，他和他所创立的王朝被称为“马其顿人”。他迁往君士坦丁堡谋求更好的生活，借娴熟的权谋和杀戮登上皇位。就文献所能让我们看到的而言，他的文化面貌完全是罗马式的，没有丝毫外来文化的痕迹，而他在位期间为他撰写的颂扬文本刻意突出他的寒微出身，把他塑造成一个新大卫。
但把这位皇帝塑成传奇人物的说法也已经开始流传。瓦西里一世去世时，他的儿子兼继承人利奥六世为他撰写了一篇葬礼演说，声称他出自阿尔萨克王朝的王室世系，而阿尔萨克王朝又出自统治着一个庞大帝国的波斯国王阿尔塔薛西斯一世（公元前465–424）。
事实上，阿尔萨克王朝起源于伊朗，只是其较晚的一支才统治了亚美尼亚。但利奥的夸耀笼罩在一桩臭名昭著的丑闻的阴影之下。牧首佛提乌被其政敌指控，在他长达十年的被废黜期间（867–877）为瓦西里伪造了一份族谱，试图通过把瓦西里的血统追溯到皈依基督教的阿尔萨克王朝亚美尼亚国王梯里达底大帝（卒于330年），来讨好瓦西里，使自己重获皇帝恩宠。
如果这个故事属实，那么利奥的葬礼演说就是基于一份伪造品。

en: In the mid-tenth century, when scholars at the court of Basileios’ grandson Konstantinos VII produced the

they fleshed this genealogy out with a full backstory, all of it definitely fictional. To make a long story short, his ancestors were ancient Armenian Arsacids who moved to the empire at the time of Leo I (457–474) and were resettled in Macedonia-Thrace. Moreover, “they preserved their ancestral nobility and prevented their

from being mixed with others” for centuries thereafter, though they occasionally intermarried with locals. Basileios was also descended from Alexander the Great and Constantine the Great—if you’re making it all up anyway, why not add them too?
zh: 十世纪中叶，当瓦西里的孙子君士坦丁七世宫廷中的学者们撰写《瓦西里一世传》时，他们为这份族谱充实了一套完整的背景故事，而这一切无疑都是虚构的。长话短说，他的祖先是古代亚美尼亚的阿尔萨克王室成员，在利奥一世（457–474）时期迁居帝国，被重新安置在马其顿—色雷斯。此外，“他们保住了祖传的贵族门第，防止自己的族类（genos）与其他族类混杂”，此后数百年皆如此，尽管他们偶尔也与当地人通婚。瓦西里还是亚历山大大帝和君士坦丁大帝的后裔——反正一切都是编造的，何不把他们也加进来呢？

en: This incredible story is the main basis for believing that Basileios was of Armenian descent. The claim was recycled in a number of later Roman and Armenian texts, but repetition does not make the original any more true. The Romans generally called Basileios a Macedonian, from his provincial origin, rather than an Armenian, and some Arabic texts call him a Slav. A fierce debate has, predictably, raged among scholars over the issue, as if there could be a single “truth” about his ancestry (the entire debate is premised on the idea of racial purity). Needless to say, the more skeptical one is of court propaganda, and the more one accepts the scandal of Photios’ forgery, the less Armenian Basileios ends up looking.

Here too the Armenian fallacy has produced its inevitable absurdities: for example, one study proposed that the eastern policies of the empress Theodora (1055–1056), Basileios’ great-great-great-granddaughter, were possibly shaped by her Armenian ancestry.
zh: 这个令人难以置信的故事，是后人认定瓦西里具有亚美尼亚血统的主要依据。这一说法在后来的一些罗马与亚美尼亚文本中被一再重复，但重复并不能使原本的说法变得更真实。罗马人通常根据瓦西里的行省出身称他为马其顿人，而非亚美尼亚人，而一些阿拉伯文本则称他为斯拉夫人。不出所料，学者们围绕这一问题展开了激烈争论，仿佛关于他的血统可能存在一个唯一的“真相”（整场争论都以种族纯洁的观念为前提）。不用说，一个人对宫廷宣传越是怀疑，越相信佛提乌伪造族谱的传闻，瓦西里就越不像亚美尼亚人。
在这里，亚美尼亚谬误也产生了其不可避免的荒谬结论：例如，一项研究提出，瓦西里的五世孙女、女皇狄奥多拉（1055–1056）的东方政策，可能受到她的亚美尼亚血统的影响。

en: In reality, Basileios’ actual ancestry is irrelevant: what matters, as always, is the politics of claims to ancestry

Basileios’ son and grandson both advertised his Armenian ancestry, without denying that he was born and raised in Macedonia, and it is likely that Basileios did so himself while he was emperor; otherwise it would be hard to explain why this odd fact was invented about him by his heirs after his death. But why might Basileios have wanted to project an Armenian royal ancestry?
zh: 事实上，瓦西里真实的血统无关紧要：真正重要的，一如既往，是人们宣称某种
背后的政治。瓦西里的儿子和孙子都宣扬他的亚美尼亚血统，同时并不否认他出生并成长于马其顿，而且很可能瓦西里本人在当皇帝时也这样做；否则就很难解释，为什么他的继承者们在他死后要为他编出这样一段奇特的身世。但瓦西里为什么会想要标榜一种亚美尼亚王室的血统呢？

en: Unfortunately, here we are in the realm of conjecture. First, we must not interpret the Armenian link apart from the others. In the fully developed version of the
Basileios is descended also from Alexander (which ennobles his Macedonian origins) and Constantine (which burnishes his Roman and imperial credentials). The legends that are told in the

about the young Basileios link him to those figures as well as to Cyrus the Great, David and Solomon, as well as to prophets of the Old Testament. We know that during his reign Basileios was eager to associate himself with those biblical figures.
The Arsacid connection was thus part of a “full-spectrum” propaganda that aimed to confer legitimacy upon this upstart in a wide variety of contexts. As it happens, the

tells of a prophecy pronounced 350 years earlier by one Isaak, another Arsacid, to the effect that an Arsacid would ascend the Roman throne. This prophesy is recorded also in (later) Armenian historiography.
zh: 遗憾的是，在这里我们进入了推测的领域。首先，我们不能把亚美尼亚这一关联与其他关联割裂开来解读。在《瓦西里一世传》详细铺陈的版本中，瓦西里还是亚历山大（这使他马其顿的出身显得高贵）和君士坦丁（这为他作为罗马人与皇帝的身份增光）的后裔。传记中关于年轻瓦西里的那些传说，把他与上述人物以及居鲁士大帝、大卫和所罗门，还有旧约的先知们联系在一起。我们知道，瓦西里在位期间热衷于把自己与那些圣经人物联系起来。
因此，阿尔萨克王朝这一关联，是一场“全方位”宣传的一部分，其目的是从多个方面证明这位出身寒微的新君有资格统治。恰好，《瓦西里一世传》记载了350年前另一位阿尔萨克王室成员伊萨克所发布的一个预言，大意是一位阿尔萨克王室成员将登上罗马皇位。这个预言也见于（后来的）亚美尼亚史学。

en: An Arsacid claim may have also given Basileios diplomatic leverage in his dealings with the empire’s Armenian neighbors, which might have worked in two ways. First, Basileios was engaged in active warfare near the borders of Armenia against the renegade Paulician sect at Tephrike, which actually had its origins in Armenia.

Second, it was during Basileios’ reign that Ašot I Bagratuni managed, through skillful diplomacy, to restore the Armenian kingship after a lapse of many centuries and have himself proclaimed king in 884. According to an almost certainly unhistorical later Armenian tradition, Basileios asked Ašot for a crown, the idea being that an Arsacid would want to be crowned by a Bagratid.
In reality, it seems instead that Basileios recognized Ašot as
of
and as his spiritual “son,” that is, as a subordinate.

An Arsacid descent would be useful in this diplomatic context. It is no coincidence that a Roman emperor claimed descent from the ancient Arsacid kings of Armenia just when the status quo in Armenia changed so dramatically.
Moreover, at this time we know that Armenian writers were also forging prestigious genealogies for their rulers, which linked them to the Assyrian and Old Testament kings.
Basileios’ genealogical fictions were perhaps meant to give him leverage.
zh: 阿尔萨克王朝的血统宣称，可能还给了瓦西里在与帝国的亚美尼亚邻邦打交道时的外交筹码，其作用可能体现在两个方面。首先，瓦西里正在亚美尼亚边境附近与据守泰弗里凯的保罗派叛离者激烈作战，而保罗派实际上起源于亚美尼亚。
其次，正是在瓦西里在位期间，阿绍特一世·巴格拉图尼凭借娴熟的外交，在许多个世纪的中断之后恢复了亚美尼亚王权，并于884年被拥立为国王。根据一个几乎可以肯定不符合史实的后来亚美尼亚传统，瓦西里曾向阿绍特求取一顶王冠，其用意是：一位阿尔萨克王室成员会想要由一位巴格拉提德王朝成员来加冕。
事实上，情况似乎相反：瓦西里承认阿绍特为众首领之首（archon of archons），并视其为自己属灵上的“儿子”，也就是一个从属者。
声称出自阿尔萨克王室，在这种外交场合可能很有用处。一位罗马皇帝恰恰在亚美尼亚的现状发生如此剧烈变化之时，宣称自己是亚美尼亚古代阿尔萨克诸王的后裔，这绝非巧合。
此外，我们知道，在这一时期亚美尼亚作家也在为他们的统治者伪造显赫的族谱，把统治者与亚述和旧约的诸王联系起来。
瓦西里那套虚构的谱系，或许就是为了在外交往来中争取主动。

en: Looking at the domestic scene, Basileios’ Armenian origins were distant enough to not threaten his Roman ethnicity (and, thereby, his ability to claim the throne) but prestigious and hoary enough to rise above the prejudice typically directed at “Armenians.” More than most people, an emperor was in a position to choose his ethnicity according to context and deploy it to his advantage both practically and symbolically. We mentioned above the

Konstantinos, the Armenian grandfather of the historian Genesios. In a rare episode of reported ethnic solidarity, Konstantinos helped Basileios at an early moment in the latter’s career, “being disposed toward him in a friendly way, as his
too was from among the Armenians.”
Interestingly, when Genesios told the same story he strengthened the connection between the two men, claiming that they were actually related.

Genesios was in effect claiming that his grandfather was related to the grandfather of the emperor to whom he was dedicating his history, Konstantinos VII. In this way, “aboriginal” claims of Armenian ethnicity could forge political links that were useful in the present, in the same way that ancient cities used Greek mythology to establish (fictional) ancestral connections when they wanted to establish closer diplomatic relations.
zh: 再看国内层面，瓦西里的亚美尼亚起源足够遥远，不至于威胁他的罗马族群性（从而也不至于威胁他宣称皇位的能力），却又足够显赫而古老，使人不至于以看待一般“亚美尼亚人”的眼光看他。比起大多数人，皇帝更有能力根据场合选择强调自己的哪一重族群背景，使它在实际上和象征意义上都有利于自己。我们上文提到过帕特里基奥斯（patrikios）君士坦丁，即史家格内西奥斯那位亚美尼亚裔祖父。在史料罕见的一则同族互助记载中，君士坦丁在瓦西里生涯的早期帮助过他，“对他怀有友善之情，因为他自己的族类（genos）也出自亚美尼亚人”。
有趣的是，格内西奥斯在讲述同一个故事时，强化了这两人之间的联系，声称他们实际上有亲属关系。
格内西奥斯实际上是在声称，自己的祖父与他所致献史书的那位皇帝——君士坦丁七世——的祖父有亲属关系。通过这种方式，声称自己的家族原出亚美尼亚，可以帮助人们建立当时有用的政治联系，正如古代城市在想要建立更密切的外交关系时，利用希腊神话来确立（虚构的）祖源联系一样。

en: The same kind of insider ethnic connection could, however, just as easily be viewed negatively, if a polemical context activated anti-Armenian prejudices. The

is extremely hostile to Stylianos Zaoutzes, the prime minister appointed by Basileios I to advise his son and heir Leon VI. The text is therefore biased when it reports that Zaoutzes’ surname was Armenian and that he was, like Basileios, a Macedonian and Armenian by
and that was why the emperor appointed him to advise his son.
Scholars are right to see this observation as a case of Roman “polemic by ethnicity.”

children: In conclusion, it cannot be doubted that thousands of Armenians lived in the empire, especially between the sixth and the eleventh centuries, served in its armies, and filled its highest offices. “The general consensus continues to be that they were the largest non-Greek unit of that society”

—so long as by “Greek” we mean “Roman.” However, the field of Byzantine Studies harbors a cottage industry that manufactures “Armenians” left and right. First, specific families and individuals are habitually given Armenian ancestry on flimsy or nonexistent grounds. Second, the field had failed to cope with the reality of assimilation: even “real” Armenians could be Romanized, just like everyone else, and we are fortunate to be able to track this process in the case of specific families over the course of a few generations. By overlooking and even sometimes rejecting the valence of Roman ethnicity in Byzantium, the field fails to distinguish between Armenians proper and Romans who had a (usually distant) Armenian ancestry—among other ancestries that the field does not privilege with the same amount of attention. This habit effaces the role of culture in shaping ethnicity and upholds an outdated racial model. Ethnic claims in Romanía, both real and invented, were political and utilitarian, not biological. It is time for us to retire biological notions of identity.

Writing this chapter came at the cost of inner conflict. I am fascinated by medieval Armenian history and believe that the Armenians are among the few actual nations of antiquity to make it through all those millennia with a more or less coherent and continuous idea about who they are, a sense that is reflected in their remarkable tradition of historiography.

Also, accounts of what Armenians suffered at the start of the twentieth century are enough to make anyone cry. Yet having been raised in a country with a strong national ideology, I can foresee exactly how this chapter will be received by some: as anti-Armenian.

This was of course not my intent. I have written this postscript in order to state my purpose directly and emphatically. This chapter calls into question an interpretation of Byzantine history propagated by Byzantinists of all nationalities. When modern Armenian historians first made these claims, they were writing at the birth of their field as a modern discipline, a hundred years ago. It was common at that time to make maximalist claims on behalf of one’s nation and claim for it the “great men” of a famous empire. But Byzantinists today should know better than to treat “race” uncritically. If my chapter speaks to current Armenian concerns, it is to debates over diaspora, the loss of identity through intermarriage and assimilation, and the degree to which the future generations of the diaspora in foreign lands still “belong” to the homeland.
总之，毋庸置疑，成千上万的亚美尼亚人生活在帝国之中，尤其是在六世纪至十一世纪之间，他们在帝国军队中服役，并充任帝国最高官职。“普遍共识仍然是：他们是那个社会中最大的非希腊人群体”

——只要我们所说的“希腊人”指的是“罗马人”。然而，拜占庭研究界却藏着一个到处给人贴标签的行当，大批造出“亚美尼亚人”。首先，一些特定的家族和个人惯常被赋予亚美尼亚血统，而其依据薄弱甚至根本不存在。其次，学界未能应对同化的现实：即便是“真正的”亚美尼亚人也可能被罗马化，就像其他所有人一样，而我们很幸运，能够在一些特定家族的案例中追踪这一过程在几代人之间的展开。由于忽视、有时甚至否认罗马族群身份在拜占庭的重要性，学界未能区分真正的亚美尼亚人与那些拥有（通常遥远的）亚美尼亚血统的罗马人——而亚美尼亚血统只是诸多血统之一，学界并未以同样的关注程度去优待其他血统。这种习惯抹去了文化在塑造族群性中的作用，维护了一种过时的种族模型。罗曼尼亚的族群宣称，无论真实的还是虚构的，都是政治性和功利性的，而非生物性的。是时候让我们摒弃生物性的身份观念了。
写本章时，我内心颇为矛盾。我对中世纪亚美尼亚历史着迷，并且相信，亚美尼亚人是古代少数几个真正延续数千年的民族之一，始终大体保有连贯而持续的自我认识，这种意识体现在他们非凡的史学传统之中。
此外，关于亚美尼亚人在二十世纪初所遭受苦难的记述，足以让任何人落泪。然而，由于在一个民族意识形态强烈的国家长大，我完全可以预想，有些人会怎样看这一章，把它看作反亚美尼亚的文章。

这当然不是我的本意。我写下这篇附言，是为了直接而郑重地表明我的目的。本章所质疑的，是一种由各国拜占庭学者所传播的拜占庭历史解释。当现代亚美尼亚历史学家最初提出这些说法时，他们是在一百年前、在其领域作为一门现代学科诞生之初写作的。在那个时代，尽量为本民族争得更多历史声名、并把一个著名帝国的“伟人”归为本民族所有，是常见的做法。但今天的拜占庭学家应当明白，不能不加批判地对待“种族”。如果说本章回应了当代亚美尼亚人的关切，那就是关于离散的种种争论：因通婚与同化而丧失身份认同，以及异国他乡的离散社群后代在多大程度上仍然“属于”故土。

en: Krumbacher, “Kasia,” 363. There is a tradition of scholarship, e.g., Kountoura-Galaki, “Armeniac Theme,” 32n35, and Vryonis, “Byzantine Images,” 69–73, which attempts to biographize the poem by linking it to an apocryphal story regarding Kasia’s participation in a bride show for Theophilos.
